title: BEYOND Phase 2
description: Amendment 0004 is hereby issued to post the Questions and Answers and a fully conformed revised solicitation. The proposal due date of the SIR is extended to October 30, 2026 at 3:00pm ET. No other changes result from Amendment 0004. __________________________________________________ Amendment 0003 is hereby issued to extend the proposal due date of the SIR to October 23, 2026 at 3:00pm ET. No other changes result from Amendment 0003. Questions and Answers are forthcoming. __________________________________________________ Amendment 0002 is hereby issued to extend the proposal due date of the SIR to October 9, 2026 at 3:00pm ET. No other changes result from Amendment 0002. Questions and Answers are forthcoming. __________________________________________________ Amendment 0001 is hereby issued to extend the proposal due date of the SIR to September 25, 2026 at 3:00pm ET. No other changes result from Amendment 0001. __________________________________________________ This is the Screening Information Request (SIR) 697DCK-26-R-00423 for the BEYOND Phase 2 Selection. This procurement is in support of the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA), Unmanned Aircraft Systems and Advanced Air Mobility Integration Office (AUS). The FAA Reauthorization Act of 2024 (P.L.118-63) Section 920 allows for the expansion of the BEYOND program. The FAA will implement a BEYOND Phase 2 competitive selection process, through this SIR. This competitive selection process is not a procurement or acquisition under the FAA Acquisition Management System. The FAA did not develop any acquisition requirements for this competitive selection process, and the process will not result in the award of a procurement contract. Consistent with the FAA Administrator�s authorities under 49 U.S.C. �106(l) and (m), this process will result in the award of an Other Transaction Agreement (OTA). The FAA intends to award up to eight (8) OTAs through this solicitation. BEYOND Phase 2 has four programmatic focus areas: infrastructure, scalability, safety and automation. Five operational focus areas have also been identified as the greatest challenges that will need to be addressed for progress to be made: public safety, controlled airspace, remote, rural areas with inadequate infrastructure, on-airport operations and cross international borders. This SIR is seeking Offerors who can deliver successful outcomesin support of the BEYOND Phase 2 focus areas. See SIR for details. The FAA intends to competitively award up to eight (8) Other Transaction Agreements (OTAs) with SLTTs in accordance with the SIR. The FAA reserves the right to execute additional OTAs if resources permit (49 U.S.C. � 106(l)). The Government will make OTA awards to the Offeror�s determined to best meet the selection criteria which are included in this SIR and reflected in the evaluation of the proposals. To be considered for award of this requirement, the Offeror must have a current/valid registration in the Systems for Award Management (SAM) database website: www.sam.gov. Registration must be active by the offer due date. Proposals must be submitted via email to the Contracting Officer and Contract Specialist no later than 3:00 pm ET on September 10, 2026. Please see attached SIR for proposal submission requirements. Questions are to be submitted, in writing, as specified in the SIR. Please reference the SIR number and BEYOND Phase 2 program on all question submissions. All questions must be received no later than 1:00pm ET on September 3, 2026. Questions will be answered in an Amendment to the SIR if deemed necessary and posted to SAM.GOV for all interested parties to consider. Prospective Offerors are encouraged to frequently visit SAM.GOV for any updates to this requirement. Any questions regarding this announcement should be directed to Kristin Frantz, Contracting Officer, at Kristin.T.Frantz@faa.gov and Jackson LeMay, Contract Specialist, at Jackson.T.Lemay@faa.gov Any proposals received after the closing date and time, will not be considered in accordance with this SIR. This SIR is not to be construed as a contract or a commitment of any kind. The Government will not be liable for payment of any costs attributed to the preparation and submission of requested proposal documentation.

title: Precision Strike Missile Increment 1
description: The Army Contracting Command � Redstone Arsenal is issuing this Sources Sought Notice as a means of conducting market research to identify manufacturing capacity and capability for production of Precision Strike Missile Increment 1 (PrSM Inc 1) follow-on production contract to support the Strategic and Operational Rockets and Missiles (STORM) Project Office. DISCLAIMER This Sources Sought Notice is for informational purposes only. This is not a request for proposal. It is a market research tool being used to determine potential firms capable of providing the supplies described herein prior to determining the method of acquisition. The Government is not obligated to and will not pay for any information received from potential sources because of this Sources Sought Notice. This does not constitute a solicitation and shall not be construed as a commitment by the Government. Responses in any form are not offers and the Government is under no obligation to award a contract as a result of this announcement. No funds are available to pay for preparation of responses to this announcement. Any information submitted by respondents to this technical description is strictly voluntary. BACKGROUND PrSM Inc 1 is a next-generation, long-range surface-to-surface ballistic missile, with launcher compatibility on M142 High Mobility Artillery Rocket System and M270 Multiple Launch Rocket Systems platforms. The purpose of this source sought notice is to conduct market research to identify potential sources with capacity and capability to produce the PrSM Inc 1 missile and pod. TECHNICAL DATA The Government retains Data Rights to Technical Data down to the Line-Replaceable Unit level and is available upon request. Technical Data is Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI) Distro D/CUI, even though the data is only CUI, to receive this information, the requestee is required to have a SECRET clearance. The Government must verify that the requestor/s are authorized (compliant at a minimal with NIST SP 800-171) and equipped to safeguard CUI and SECRET information. This is a multi-step process that requires a minimum of 3-5 business days. Interested parties must provide the following information prior to accessing the technical data. Send requests to: Contract Specialist, Gregory Walcott, at gregory.n.walcott.civ@army.mil and Contracting Officer Monica Clemons, at monica.e.clemons.civ@army.mil. Provide CAGE code that verifies SECRET status and submit requests for access through the SAM.GOV website. The Government will review the National Industrial Security System (NISS) to confirm if the company network/system is authorized to house CUI information. Any interested party for which �SECRET� facility clearance cannot be verified through the NISS will be denied access. All requests for documents shall be made at least 5 business days prior to the Sources Sought Notice closing. Requests made after this time will be processed but extensions to the Sources Sought Notice will not be considered and submission is still required prior to closing. Once �SECRET� facility clearance is verified, the attachments will be made available. REQUIRED CAPABILITIES The STORM Project Office seeks to gauge the industrial base for skills, capacity and capability for production of the PrSM Inc 1. This information will be used to identify possible sources and help shape decisions for follow on efforts. Interested vendors are requested to provide information regarding their capabilities to provide a weapon system (or key subsystems) with the following characteristics (at a minimum): Manufacturing Capability (The "How"): Describe your processes of basic tasks resources, and exclusive agreements that are required to produce missiles of similar complexity as the PrSM Inc 1. Reliability and Maintainability: Describe how your company will achieve high operational availability while maintaining minimal maintenance. Facilities & Advanced Equipment: Provide the total square footage, cleanrooms, specialized tooling, and machinery. Technical & Workforce Qualifications: Specify your certifications (e.g., AS9100, ISO 9001, and DoD Manual 4145.26 etc.). It is expected to already have facilities and personnel to support classified requirements. Digital Engineering & Open Architecture: Explain current IT Architecture Efficiencies, implementation of Modular Open Systems Approach Integration, design to facilitate integration with future platforms to include foreign partners. Cybersecurity: Compliant with current cybersecurity standards for weapon systems Cyber Supply Chain Risk Management, IAW DoDI 8500.01, DoDI 5200.44, NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5, DODI 8510.01 Risk Management Framework CNSSI 1253 and DFARS 254-204-7012, NIST SP 800-171 Rev.3. Personnel and Facility Security Clearances: Obtain a DD Form 254 Contract Security Classification Specification. The prime contractor processing CLASSIFIED information shall obtain a minimum �Secret Clearance� completing a Standard Form 86. The contractor�s facility shall have and maintain facility authorization to operate issued by Defense Counterintelligence and Security Agency. National Security Compliance: with United States laws and regulations on �Export Control,� including the International Traffic in Arms Regulations and the Export Administration Regulations. ELIGIBILITY The applicable North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code for this requirement is 336414. The Product Service Code is 1410. Businesses of all sizes are encouraged to respond; however, each respondent must clearly identify their business size in their capabilities statement and address the capabilities above and below. ADDITIONAL INFORMATION AND SUBMISSION DETAILS (CAPABILITIES STATEMENT) The requested information is to assist the Government in conducting market research to determine potential business sources that have the assets, skills, experience, financial stability, qualifications, and requisite knowledge required to support the requirement. A determination not to compete this proposed action based upon responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government. It is requested that interested businesses submit to the contracting office a capabilities statement package (no more than 10 pages in length, Times New Roman 12-point font minimum) The capabilities statement should demonstrate the ability to perform the tasking listed under the required capabilities above and items 1-3 below. The Government prefers responses addressing all stated content below and up above in Required Capability. However, even if all content cannot be addressed, the Government still encourages responses that provide a description of strength areas and is a beneficial contribution. Responding to a subset of the items below: Provide Rough Order of Magnitude: pricing for any required /Integrator capability and platform compatibility at various quantities. Provide a Description: of the potential program organization and resourcing plan addressing any innovative solutions to support a collaborative government-industry partnership. Describe Past Experience: Missile System Integration & Supply Chain Management and Risk Mitigation plan. All responses under this Sources Sought Notice need to request a DODSAFE drop from the designated Contract Specialist, Gregory Walcott, at gregory.n.walcott.civ@army.mil and Contracting Officer Monica Clemons, at monica.e.clemons.civ@army.mil. All responses shall be unclassified. All data received in response to this Sources Sought Notice that is marked or designated as corporate or proprietary will be fully protected from any release outside the U.S. Government (USG). No phone calls will be accepted. All questions must be submitted to the Contract Specialist and Contracting Officer identified above. The USG is not committed nor obligated to pay for the information provided, and no basis for claims against the USG shall arise as a result of a response to this Sources Sought

title: SPE4A727R0094 � 1650-015420178 - ARMATURE ASSY,MOTOR - AIRCRAFT, OSPREY V-22
description: The Defense Logistics Agency is issuing this sources sought synopsis as a means of conducting market research to identify parties having an interest in and the resources to support this requirement for NSN: 1650-015420178, ARMATURE ASSY,MOTOR. This item is currently identified as part number RTX CORPORATION 55820 P/N 4951533-1 SKURKA AEROSPACE INC 95270 P/N 4951533-1 or 5492D110 BELL BOEING JOINT PROJECT OFFICE 3B1R2 P/N 4951533-1. Potential sources shall be capable of furnishing all labor, materials, facilities and equipment required to accomplish the new manufacture of the item(s). Generally, this entails the procurement/manufacture of component parts, inspection, testing, preservation/packaging, and shipping. Additionally, potential sources may be responsible for supply chain management, logistics planning, forecasting production requirements, long-lead time parts procurement, diminishing manufacturing sources and material shortage issues, and shipping serviceable assets. If significant subcontracting or teaming is anticipated in order to deliver technical capability, organizations should address the administrative and management structure of such arrangements. The government will evaluate market information to ascertain potential market capacity to 1) provide services consistent in scope and scale with those described in this notice and otherwise anticipated; 2) secure and apply the full range of corporate financial, human capital, and technical resources required to successfully perform similar requirements; 3) implement a successful project management plan that includes: compliance with tight program schedules; cost containment; meeting and tracking performance; hiring and retention of key personnel and risk mitigation; and 4) provide services under a performance based service acquisition contract. BASED ON THE RESPONSES TO THIS SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE/MARKET RESEARCH, THIS REQUIREMENT MAY BE SET-ASIDE FOR SMALL BUSINESSES OR PROCURED THROUGH FULL AND OPEN COMPETITION, and multiple awards MAY be made. Telephone inquiries will not be accepted or acknowledged, and no feedback or evaluations will be provided to companies regarding their submissions. Submission Instructions: Interested parties who consider themselves qualified to perform the above-listed services are invited to submit a response to this Sources Sought Notice by October 30, 2026 3:00 pm eastern standard time. To submit your SAR please send an email to: dlaavnsmallbus@dla.mil, subject line "Request a SAR drop off". Include CAGE code, the NSN and the email address where you want to receive the DoDSafe link. After your email is received, a DoDSafe drop off will be returned, where you can download your SAR file.

title: P7777 ACC SARP Replacement NAS Jacksonville, Florida - Metasys
description: Notice of intent to use a brand name product. The Naval Facilities Engineering Systems Command, Southeast (NAVFAC SE) is performing a market survey to determine if other potential sources of supply can provide a building automation control system that has equal performance to the Metasys, manufactured by Johnson Controls, Carretera Reynosa-Matamoros Brecha E 99, Km 3 Reynosa, Tamaulipas, CP 88780 Mexico. Fiscal Year 2027 PROJECT P7777 ACC SARP Replacement NAS Jacksonville, Florida, requires the following characteristics. Provide a building automation control system with the following characteristics: Scalability � Provide seamlessly connection of field controllers to supervisory servers with no unnecessary intermediate hardware or components. Open Integration � Provide true protocol openness, allowing third-party equipment and legacy devices to run on the same platform. Supports industry protocol standards including BACnet. Security � Provide encrypted communications, multi-factor authentication, and a secure user role management program. Interface Dashboard � Provide facility managers with a centralized interface that flags active security risks, system vulnerabilities, and actionable mitigation guidance. Integration with Existing System � Provide seamless connectivity to the existing Johnson Control Metasys system currently serving the main hospital (Bldg 2080) at NAS Jacksonville. Seamless connectivity ensures all monitored and controlled points at the building are fully visible and accessible by the Metasys control system serving the main hospital. This notification is for market research purposes only to identify if other potential sources of supply can meet the requirements of the Government. This is not a request for proposals, quotes, or an invitation for bid. The intent of this notice is to identify other potential sources of this product. To be considered, please submit detailed technical data for the Government to conduct a comprehensive evaluation of your manufactured product to ensure compatibility with the existing system. In accordance with FAR 15.201(e), a response to this notice is not an offer and cannot be accepted by the Government to form a binding contract. The responder is solely responsible for the information it submits and any associated costs. The Government reserves the right to disregard any submittal that is incomplete or vague. Please do not submit company brochures. Please limit your submissions to five (5) one-sided pages, not including the cover or table of contents pages. In addition, Attachment 1 must be included with your submission, and does not count against the page limit. Please submit complete information via electronic mail to Reuben Amarh reuben.a.amarh.civ@us.navy.mil and Jeff Rhein at jeffrey.j.rhein.civ@us.navy.mil no later than 30 OCT 2026 at 3:00 PM ET. Any information received after the due date/time will not be considered. Any information provided to the Government in response to this RFI will become U.S. Government property. All proprietary or classified information will be treated appropriately.

title: Government-Owned, Contactor-Operated (GOCO) and Contractor-Owned/Contractor-Operated (COCO) fuel services at Marine Corps Air Ground Combat Center 29 Palms, CA
description: SOLICITATION SPE603-26-R-0543 Government-Owned, Contactor-Operated (GOCO) and Contractor-Owned/Contractor-Operated (COCO) fuel services at Marine Corps Air Ground Combat Center 29 Palms, CA Defense Logistics Agency (DLA) - Energy - FESAB is issuing a Request for Proposal (RFP) for Government-Owned, Contractor-Operated (GOCO) and Contractor Owned, Contractor-Operated (COCO) Fuel Storage, Operations, and Distribution services at Marine Corps Air Ground Combat Center (MCAGCC) 29 Palms, CA. The Contractor will be responsible for the management, operation, maintenance, product quality surveillance, inventory control and accounting, security, safety, and environmental protection of the Marine Corps GOCO and COCO fuel facilities. The Contractor will ensure safe, accurate, and timely handling, quality control, and accountability of all Defense Wide Working Capital Fund (DWWCF)-owned petroleum products under their control. The Contractor will perform required maintenance to ensure facilities, associated systems, vehicles, and equipment remain operational to meet the base mission. The Contractor will comply with environmental protection, safety, and security directives. The Contractor will conduct required training to ensure personnel are fully qualified to perform Performance Work Statement (PWS) tasks. The contractor must receive, maintain, store, sample and test, internal transfer, and issue petroleum products. The contractor must be responsible for all fuel-servicing operations and safeguarding facilities, equipment, and fuel products under its control during normal and adverse conditions. The contractor must track aviation fuels inventories and order products as needed to meet DLA Energy Accounting Policies and maintain levels to ensure uninterrupted service. This procurement is 100% set aside for Service-Disabled Veteran Owned Business (SDVOSB) under NAICS code 493190 (Other Warehouse and Storage). The Government anticipates awarding a firm fixed-price contract. The Period of Performance (PoP) will be from March 15, 2028 � September 14, 2031 (COCO PoP 3.5-yearbase), September 15, 2028 � September 14, 2031 (GOCO PoP 3-year base), four, five-year option periods from September 15, 2031 � September 14, 2036 (1st Option); September 15,2036 � September 14, 2041 (2nd Option); September 15, 2041 � September 14, 2046 (3rdOption); September 15, 2046 � September 14, 2051 (4th Option), one, 4.5-year option period from September 15, 2051 - March 14, 2056 (5th Option); and an option to extend the contract not to exceed six (6) months from March 15, 2056 through September 14, 2056. This procurement will be solicited under full and open competition after exclusion of sources in accordance with FAR 6.206, Set-Asides for service-disabled veteran-owned small business (SDVOSB) concerns eligible under the SDVOSB Program and FAR 19.14, Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business Program. Interested companies responding to the solicitation will be required to register in the System for Award Management (SAM) and Procurement Integrated Enterprise Environment (PIEE). Amendment 0001 issued on August 27, 2026.

title: J061--541 Electrical Power Distribution Equipment Testing, Inspection, and Maintenance - VAMC Cleveland
description: The purpose of this amendment is to provide answers to the questions received prior to the cutoff date. In addition to providing answer to the questions, a site visit is also set for 0900 on Tuesday 27 October 2026 at the Louis Stokes Cleveland VA Medical Center 10701 East Boulevard, Cleveland, Ohio 44106-1702. We will meet at the information desk, first floor of the Atrium. This is directly across from the parking garage. Is this a new requirement or a recompete? If a recompete, please identify the incumbent contractor, the previous contract number, and the prior contract value. The final option year of the previous contract 36C25022F0010 has expired. Can prior test reports (most recent tri-annual cycle, IR survey, oil analysis) be provided to help establish equipment condition and test history? Prior test reports will not be shared outside of authorized staff. What is the estimated contract value or funding range for this requirement? This is not a construction requirement and therefore we do not have a project magnitude. The circuit breaker testing schedules for Option Year 1 (November 1, 2027 October 31, 2028) and Option Year 4 (November 1, 2030 October 31, 2031) appear to omit the quantity column shown in the other annual schedules. Could the Government provide revised schedules identifying the quantities for each listed circuit breaker in these two option years? Edited spreadsheet for breaker listing provided below. The SOW identifies working hours of 7:00 a.m. 11:30 p.m. Monday through Friday and 6:00 a.m. 6:00 p.m. Saturday and Sunday when maintenance requires an electrical power interruption. However, we could not locate an equipment schedule distinguishing Normal (Monday Friday) equipment from Critical (Saturday Sunday) equipment. Could the Government provide this classification or confirm how contractors should determine which equipment requires weekend work for pricing purposes? Any work that requires power to be interrupted will be completed on Sunday s, during daylight hours. Work that does not require power interruption, i.e. IR scan or transformer oil samples can be completed M-F during normal working hours. The section requires electrical contracting to be the primary specialty of the contractor's business and references properly trained and licensed permanent staff. Would the VA consider a qualified small-business prime contractor that provides contract management, coordination, quality assurance, and oversight while utilizing an experienced electrical testing subcontractor with the required NETA certifications, licensed personnel, equipment, and relevant past performance? This requirement is intended for contractors whose primary business specialty is electrical testing, inspection, maintenance, and repair of electrical power distribution systems. The Government expects the prime contractor to possess the technical qualifications, experience, and personnel necessary to directly perform the primary work requirements identified in this SOW. While the use of subcontractors is not prohibited, the Government does not intend for the prime contractor's role to be limited solely to contract administration, quality assurance, and oversight while substantially all technical work is performed by a subcontractor. Offerors shall comply with all applicable subcontracting and performance requirements identified in the solicitation and applicable regulations. Technician certification equivalence: the statement of work requires technicians certified to NETA standards or an equivalent certifying organization. Would NICET-certified technicians performing testing to the latest NETA MTS standards be accepted as equivalent for this requirement? NICET-certified technicians may be accepted as meeting the "equivalent certifying organization" requirement, provided the certification is in a relevant electrical testing, maintenance, or power-distribution-related subfield and the individual possesses the knowledge, training, and experience necessary to perform the testing, inspection, maintenance, and troubleshooting activities required under this contract. Consistent with the SOW requirements, personnel performing the work shall have a minimum of five (5) years of relevant documented experience and shall perform all testing in accordance with the latest edition of the NETA Maintenance Testing Specifications (MTS). Additionally, NICET Level III or higher in an applicable electrical power testing or power distribution discipline will be considered equivalent to the NETA certification requirement. Additionally, would the VA consider the subcontractor's technical qualifications and past performance when evaluating the prime contractor's technical capability? This requirement is intended for contractors whose primary business specialty is electrical testing, inspection, maintenance, and repair of electrical power distribution systems. The Government expects the prime contractor to possess the technical qualifications, experience, and personnel necessary to directly perform the primary work requirements identified in this SOW. While subcontractors may be utilized as permitted by the solicitation, the Government does not intend for the prime contractor's role to be limited solely to contract administration, quality assurance, and oversight while substantially all technical work is performed by a subcontractor. Evaluation of technical capability and past performance will be conducted in accordance with the evaluation criteria specified in the solicitation. Finally, please confirm which limitation on subcontracting applies to this procurement under NAICS 238210. The NAICS for this requirement is 238210 Offer due date: The SAM.gov notice header lists a response date of October 19, 2026, but the solicitation text says quotes are due October 23, 2026 at 3:00 PM ET. Please confirm which date and time govern. SAM was corrected within 4 hours of the posting to reflect 10/23/2026 at 15:00 which matches the solicitation that was posted. Period of performance: The SOW lists a base year of November 1, 2026 through October 31, 2027, plus four option years. Please confirm the anticipated award date that supports a November 1 start. The current need is to start 11/1/2026. The period of performance will start as soon as possible if not on 11/1/2026. The SOW requires NETA-certified technicians "or equivalent." Please confirm whether the certification may be held by the subcontractor's technicians doing the testing, and which other certifications are acceptable as equivalent. The Government expects the prime contractor to possess the technical qualifications, experience, and personnel necessary to directly perform the primary testing, inspection, maintenance, and troubleshooting activities required under this contract. The use of qualified subcontractors is permitted; however, the prime contractor shall maintain an active onsite role and directly perform a substantial portion of the work with its own qualified personnel. The prime contractor's role shall not be limited solely to contract administration, project management, quality assurance, or oversight functions. For personnel qualification purposes, NETA-certified technicians are acceptable. As an equivalent certification, the Government will accept NICET Level III or higher certification in an applicable electrical power testing or power distribution discipline, provided the technician has a minimum of five (5) years of documented relevant experience and performs testing in accordance with the latest edition of the NETA Maintenance Testing Specifications (MTS). Limitations on subcontracting: The solicitation includes FAR 52.219-14. Please confirm that the services limit applies (no more than 50% of the amount paid may go to subcontractors that are not similarly situated). Yes the clause applies to this requirement. Solicitation number W911N226QA034 will be released on or about 18 September 2026, with a closing date on or about 30 October 2026. description: Notice of intent to use a brand name product. The Naval Facilities Engineering Systems Command, Southeast (NAVFAC SE) is performing a market survey to determine if other potential sources of supply can provide a ligature-resistant sliding door system that has equal performance to the LR-SDS / SL-LR-SDS, manufactured by Accurate Lock & Hardware, 1 Annie Place, Stamford, CT 06902. Fiscal Year 2027 PROJECT P7777 ACC SARP Replacement NAS Jacksonville, Florida, requires the following characteristics. Provide ligature-resistant sliding door system with the following capabilities: Ligature-Resistant Design � A sliding door system specifically designed for behavioral health environments that eliminates ligature opportunities associated with conventional swinging doors, including the top edge of the door and side latch locations. The system shall utilize a concealed overhead track, concealed locking hardware, ligature-resistant operating trim, and concealed vertical rod locking or latching mechanisms with no exposed anchor points or accessible cavities. Threshold and Floor Guide � An anti-barricade floor guide that allows sliding operation without creating additional ligature points. Optional threshold/transom assemblies shall be available to reduce the bottom door gap while allowing emergency access and maintaining safe operation. Safety and Security Features � The system shall reduce opportunities for patient barricading, prevent the door from being used as a swinging weapon, and provide staff override capability for all interior locking functions. Locking functions shall include behavioral health applications such as classroom, storeroom, and self-latching patient room configurations. Performance Requirements � The system shall: Meet or exceed a 150 ft-lb impact test in accordance with ANSI A250.13-2014, Section 6.1.1.2. Continue to function following impact testing. Utilize dual ball-bearing carrier assemblies rated at 1,240 lbs dynamic load capacity each. Where required, comply with ANSI/UL 1784 air leakage testing with measured leakage substantially below the allowable code limit. Unique Product Characteristics � The system incorporates proprietary concealed track, locking, and staff-override hardware specifically developed for behavioral healthcare applications. The integrated design combines ligature resistance, anti-barricade functionality, smoke-control capability (where required), and behavioral health locking functions within a single system. The LR-SDS has also been evaluated by the New York State Office of Mental Health and is included in the OMH Patient Safety Guidelines. title: Data at Rest (DaR) - 400 Obsolescence Resolution
description: OBJECTIVE: The USAF E-3G AWACS provides worldwide response to situations requiring immediate and continuous on-scene command, control, and battle management using embedded real-time surveillance to support employment of U.S. and allied combat forces. The E-3G consists of the air vehicle, sensor systems, and computing and communications equipment. The current USAF E-3G operational fleet consists of 15 operational aircraft. The E-3G DAR-400 (part numbers 63-2824652-01 through -03) is a mission critical asset and is in critical need of obsolescence resolution to prevent mission impact. Since the DAR-400 contains encrypted MCS, MSS, IPEC and GS data, a failure would directly impact operations and data security. General Dynamics Mission Systems (GDMS) has notified us that the DAR-400 will not be able to support or upgrade to changing NSA requirements. SCOPE: To execute the installation and integration of the obsolescence resolution for the mission-critical E-3G DAR-400 to prevent mission impact. The provided Government-owned KG-204 based solution is compliant with current DoD and NSA mandates to replace the legacy DAR-400 equipment. REQUEST FOR INFORMATION DETAILS: 1. AFLCMC/WIW is requesting information from industry as part of market research to determine interest level and size of qualified vendors. 2. THIS IS A SOURCES SOUGHT ONLY. It is not a Request for Proposal, a Request for Quotation, an Invitation for Bid, a solicitation, or an indication the US Air Force (AF) or AFLCMC/WIW will contract for the items contained in the sources sought. AFLCMC/WIW will not pay respondents for information provided in response to the sources sought. 3. The Government is requesting information from vendors of all business sizes including socioeconomic programs such as 8(a), Historically Underutilized Business Zone (HUBZone), Women Owned Small Business, or Service-Disabled Veteran Owned Small Businesses (SDVOSB) that are interested in performing this requirement. The Government requests interested parties submit a brief description of their company�s business size (i.e., annual revenues and employee size), business status (i.e., 8(a), HUBZone, or SDVOSB, Women Owned Small Business, or small business), and any anticipated teaming arrangements. The Government will use this information in determining its small business set-aside decision. 4. Interested parties should submit a capabilities package, with a cover letter, that is brief and concise yet clearly demonstrates ability to meet the stated requirements with sufficiently qualified personnel. Provide qualification information (type and duration of employee experience relevant to the requirements) and the level of involvement (prime or sub-contractor) and time periods for work on similar projects. The capabilities package should clearly present evidence that the interested party is fully capable of providing the required services and as such may contain any information that the interested party feels relevant. 5. Responses should be submitted electronically, and must be no more than ten single-spaced pages, using 12-point, Times New Roman font, and minimum one-inch margins, in Microsoft Word format. Responses that only provide a company website will not be considered. 6. Responses to the sources sought are requested by 3PM, CDT, 12 October 2026. All responses shall be unclassified and reviewed to ensure consideration. All responses, correspondence, and/or questions related to this matter should be e-mailed to: E-mail: phaedra.prather@us.af.mil Phone: (405) 739-4340 Attachments: DAR 400 Follow On SOW_Sep 2026 DAR Follow-On draft CDRL_DID Package 2026

description: THIS IS A PROJECT LABOR AGREEMENT (PLA) NOTICE TO BE USED FOR MARKET ANALYSIS ONLY. NO AWARDS WILL BE MADE FROM THE RESPONSES TO THIS SYNOPSIS. NO REIMBURSEMENT WILL BE MADE FOR ANY COSTS ASSOCIATED WITH PROVIDING INFORMATION IN RESPONSE TO THIS SYNOPSIS OR ANY FOLLOW UP INFORMATION REQUESTS. NO SOLICITATION WILL BE AVAILABLE AT THIS TIME; HOWEVER, RESPONSES WILL BE USED TO DETERMINE THE APPROPRIATE ACQUISITION STRATEGY FOR A FUTURE ACQUISITION. NO RESPONSES TO THIS PLA NOTICE WILL BE POSTED TO SAM.GOV. The purpose of this announcement is to gain knowledge of the use and benefits of Project Labor Agreements (PLAs), Liberty State Park Ecosystem Restoration Project located in Jersey City, NJ. The NAICS Code is 237990 (Other Heavy and Civil Engineering Construction). Any potential solicitation(s) that may proceed from this notice will be posted to sam.gov. All interested offerors will have the opportunity to respond to a solicitation announcement later if a solicitation is issued. BACKGROUND AND INFORMATION FOR CONSTRUCTION CONTRACT The New York District, U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (District) is preparing plans and specifications for construction of the Liberty State Park Ecosystem Restoration Project located in Jersey City, NJ. The goal of the project is to create a resilient coastal ecosystem within a highly urbanized setting that provides both ecological and social benefits. Primary project components include: Restoration of the Liberty State Park interior including approximately 46.2 acres of tidal wetland habitat, 25.0 acres of non-tidal wetland habitat, and 72.6 acres of native upland habitat. Enhancement of approximately 7.1 acres of existing non-tidal wetland (4.5 acres) and upland (2.6 acres) habitats by removing invasive flora and planting native species. Creation of park amenities to accommodate and provide public interaction with this habitat restoration project, such as trail networks, overlooks, bird blinds, viewing hills, and a restroom. The State of New Jersey, acting through the New Jersey Department of Environmental Protection (NJDEP), is the non-Federal sponsor for this project. The magnitude of the Liberty State Park Ecosystem Restoration project is between $100,000,000 and $250,000,000. The duration of construction is anticipated to be approximately 1,686 calendar days after Notice to Proceed. Notice to Proceed is anticipated to occur approximately in October 2027. Responses to this source sought will be used by the Government to help determine whether the use of a PLA will achieve economy and efficiency in the completion of the subject project. All firms and labor unions should respond to this announcement if they are interested in performing the work for this project. PLA DEFINITION A PLA is defined as a pre-hire collective bargaining agreement with one or more labor organizations that establishes the terms and conditions of employment for a specific construction project and is an agreement described in 29 U.S.C. 158(f). FEDERAL ACQUISITION REGULATION (FAR) SUBPART 22.503 - POLICY Executive Order (E.O.) 14063, Use of Project Labor Agreements for Federal Construction Projects, requires agencies to use project labor agreements in large-scale construction projects to promote economy and efficiency in the administration and completion of Federal construction projects. When awarding a contract in connection with a large-scale construction project (see 22.502), agencies shall require use of project labor agreements for contractors and subcontractors engaged in construction on the project, unless an exception at 22.504(d) applies. An agency may require the use of a project labor agreement on projects where the total cost to the Federal Government is less than that for a large-scale construction project, if appropriate. An agency may, if appropriate, require that every contractor and subcontractor engaged in construction on the project agree, for that project, to negotiate or become a party to a project labor agreement with one or more labor organizations if the agency decides that the use of project labor agreements will Advance the Federal Government's interest in achieving economy and efficiency in Federal procurement, producing labor-management stability, and ensuring compliance with laws and regulations governing safety and health, equal employment opportunity, labor and employment standards, and other matters; and Be consistent with law. Agencies may consider the following factors in deciding whether the use of a project labor agreement is appropriate for a construction project where the total cost to the Federal Government is less than that for a large-scale construction project: The project will require multiple construction contractors and/or subcontractors employing workers in multiple crafts or trades. There is a shortage of skilled labor in the region in which the construction project will be sited. Completion of the project will require an extended period of time. Project labor agreements have been used on comparable projects undertaken by Federal, State, municipal, or private entities in the geographic area of the project. A project labor agreement will promote the agency's long term program interests, such as facilitating the training of a skilled workforce to meet the agency's future construction needs. Any other factors that the agency decides are appropriate. For indefinite-delivery indefinite-quantity (IDIQ) contracts the use of a project labor agreement may be required on an order-by-order basis rather than for the entire contract. For an order at or above $35 million an agency shall require the use of a project labor agreement unless an exception applies. See 22.504(d)(3) and 22.505(b)(3). PLA COMMENT SOLICITATION In consideration of the above factors, and any others which may be deemed appropriate, the construction community is invited to comment on the use of PLAs. Of particular interest to the Government are responses to the following questions: Have comparable projects been undertaken by Federal, State, municipal, or private entities in the geographic area of this project? For each project, please indicate if a PLA was used, the initial and final cost if available, number of trades on the project, if the project was completed on time, and if there were any challenges such as labor shortages, labor related delays, safety issues, etc. Are you aware of skilled labor shortages in the area for those crafts that will be needed to complete the referenced project? Certification: American Registry for Diagnostic Medical Sonography (ARDMS) required for all Ultrasound Technicians. All Contractor s Ultrasound Technicians must be currently certified in Basic Life Support (BLS), Advanced Cardiac Life Support (ACLS) or equivalency. All continuing education courses required for maintaining certification must always be kept up to date. Documentation verifying current certification must be provided by the Contractor to the VA COR on an annual basis for each year of contract performance. The Contractor is responsible for ensuring that proposed technicians(s) possess the requisite credentials enabling the granting of privileges. title: Upcoming Construction Opportunity: Land Port of Entry Highgate Springs, VT
description: THIS IS A SPECIAL NOTICE OF AN ANTICIPATED PROCUREMENT. THIS IS NOT A SOLICITATION OR REQUEST FOR PROPOSALS. The U.S. General Services Administration (GSA), Public Buildings Service, is issuing this Special Notice to provide advance notification of an upcoming construction procurement for the new Land Port of Entry in Highgate Springs, Vermont. GSA had previously planned to use the Construction Manager as Constructor (CMc) delivery method. GSA now anticipates proceeding with a separate construction procurement using the Design-Bid-Build (DBB) delivery method, with construction services provided by a General Contractor (GC) at a firm fixed price. This notice is intended to inform interested industry participants of the anticipated opportunity and the planned change in delivery method, as well as to request statements from interested vendor candidates. Project Location Land Port of Entry Highgate Springs, Vermont Project Description The anticipated procurement is for construction services associated with the new Land Port of Entry in Highgate Springs, Vermont, along the United States�Canada border. The project is being undertaken by GSA to provide modern border infrastructure in support of the operational, security, and facility requirements of the Federal agencies responsible for border inspection and processing. Constructed in 1997, the existing Highgate Springs Land Port of Entry is at the northern end of U.S. Interstate 89 (I- 89), approximately 40 miles north of Burlington, Vermont, and opposite the Canadian port of entry at St. Armand/Philipsburg, Quebec. Canada is completing construction of Autoroute A-35 between Montreal and the Canada/U.S. border. Canada in coordination with Vermont�s Agency of Transportation is converting Route 133 into a multilane highway, which would link Montreal to the US border with a continuous multilane highway. When completed, traffic is estimated to increase by as much as 30% at this port of entry. The existing site occupies approximately 16.1 acres and includes seven buildings totaling approximately 44,000 gross square feet. The site is bounded to the north by the U.S./Canada border, to the east by the northbound lanes of I-89 and rock outcroppings and bluffs, to the south by the former site of the State of Vermont�s Welcome Center, and to the west by privately owned land. Lake Champlain is about 1/2 mile to the west. Tenants include the U.S. Department of Homeland Security�s Customs and Border Protection ; the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services� Food and Drug Administration; the U.S. Department of Agriculture�s Animal and Plant Health Inspection Service, and GSA. This project will construct a new fully operational Land Port of Entry at Highgate Springs with expanded capacity to alleviate the increase in commercial and personally owned vehicle (POV) traffic expected upon the completion of Canada�s A-35 expansion project. The project is intended to deliver a modern, functional, secure, and efficient land port of entry that supports the movement of people and goods while meeting applicable Federal facility standards, building codes and security requirements. The anticipated construction scope includes the labor, materials, equipment, supervision, coordination, and other resources necessary to complete the work in accordance with the contract documents. The final scope of work, project requirements, and construction specifications will be provided in a forthcoming solicitation. Anticipated Delivery Method Design-Bid-Build / General Contractor GSA anticipates procuring construction services through a Design-Bid-Build delivery method. Under this approach, the construction contractor will perform the work in accordance with the completed design and the requirements established in the solicitation and resulting contract at a firm-fixed price. The forthcoming solicitation will establish the acquisition strategy, contract requirements, evaluation criteria, and instructions for submitting offers. Anticipated Procurement GSA anticipates issuing a competitive solicitation for the construction phase of the Highgate Springs Land Port of Entry project. The solicitation is anticipated to be published on SAM.gov in November 2026. The anticipated schedule is subject to change. Interested firms are encouraged to monitor SAM.gov for the forthcoming solicitation and any subsequent procurement announcements. The full description of the work, construction requirements, anticipated schedule, contract terms, and proposal submission instructions will be provided in the solicitation. Vendor Response and Requested Interested vendors are requested to submit a brief statement outlining their qualifications, relevant project experience, and interest in this project to the Point of Contact listed below by October 30, 2026. This notice is not a solicitation, invitation for bids, or request for proposals. Submissions should be sent directly to the Point of Contact listed below. This notice does not commit the Government to issue a solicitation, award a contract, or proceed with the anticipated procurement. Any procurement will be conducted in accordance with the solicitation and applicable acquisition requirements. GSA will not reimburse any costs incurred by interested parties in connection with this notice. Point of Contact Questions concerning this Special Notice may be directed to: David Mazzolini Senior Contracting Officer General Services Administration, Public Buildings Service Email: david.mazzolini@gsa.gov Interested parties should refer to the forthcoming solicitation on SAM.gov for official procurement information, requirements, and instructions.

title: Europe South District Playground Inspection, Maintenance, and Repair
description: The Department of War Education Activity (DoWEA) is one of only two federally operated school systems in the United States. DoWEA plans, directs, coordinates, and manages pre-kindergarten through grade 12 educational programs on behalf of the Department of War (DoW). DoWEA operates approximately 165 brick-and-mortar schools across eight districts located in seven U.S. states, eleven foreign countries, Guam, and Puerto Rico, serving more than 72,000 students worldwide. DoWEA Europe consists of multiple districts encompassing schools, District Superintendent Offices (DSOs), and Student Transportation Offices (STOs) supporting children of active-duty military members and eligible civilian employees. The Contractor shall provide full-service, performance-based playground inspection, preventive maintenance, repair, emergency response, cleaning services for DoWEA facilities located in Europe South Region. For the purposes of this PWS, playgrounds include all playground systems and associated features, whether standalone or co-located, including but not limited to: Playground equipment and structures; Playground surfacing systems; Hard-surface and multi-use play courts; Outdoor recreational and athletic surfaces; and, Perimeter features, furnishings, and appurtenances. The Contractor shall furnish all management, supervision, labor, tools, equipment, materials, transportation, documentation, and incidentals necessary to ensure playgrounds remain safe, serviceable, compliant, and operational throughout the period of performance.

title: 6530--Rehabilitation Equipment - High Low Beds and Parallel Bars - for the East Indianapolis VA clinic
description: SOURCE SOUGHT NOTICE Rehabilitation Equipment High Low Beds and Parallel Bars This announcement requests information from industry to support market research and preliminary acquisition planning for the procurement of physical therapy/rehabilitation equipment needed for a new clinic near Indianapolis, IN. The purpose of this notice is to assess industry interest and identify potential sources with the capabilities and qualifications to meet the following requirements. This is not a solicitation for quotes. No contract will be awarded from this notice. No proposals are being requested or accepted with this notice. The government will not pay any costs for the time and effort to respond to this notice. REQUIREMENT The agency is seeking information on domestic sources of supply for two pieces of medical equipment as described below: Parallel Bars, Physical Therapy (quantity 1 each) Description: The electric platform-mounted parallel bars shall provide adjustable support for gait training, balance, mobility, and rehabilitation activities. The system shall provide powered height adjustment, adjustable width, a slip-resistant walking platform, and stable handrails to accommodate patients of varying sizes and functional abilities. Salient Characteristics: Made in America. Provides a 10-foot gait-training platform. Provides 500 lb load capacity. Electrically adjusts handrail height from approximately 26 54 in. Manually adjusts handrail width from approximately 20 34 in. Includes 1.5-in. diameter stainless-steel handrails. Includes a 48-in. wide, two-piece slip-resistant platform. Provides digital height display and four programmable height settings. Provides synchronized powered height adjustment with automatic safety shutoff. Equipment shall be new, current-production equipment suitable for professional rehabilitation applications. ETL approved. Table, Treatment, Hi-Lo, Bariatric, 500-lb capacity (quantity 3 each) Description: The bariatric hi-lo treatment table shall provide a stable, electrically powered treatment surface for patient examination, evaluation, rehabilitation, and therapeutic procedures. The table shall support safe patient transfers through powered height adjustment while providing multiple positioning options to accommodate a wide range of clinical applications. The system shall be suitable for physical therapy, occupational therapy, rehabilitation, outpatient clinics, sports medicine, and VA healthcare facilities. Salient Characteristics: Made in America Provides a powered height-adjustable treatment surface with a height range of approximately 18 to 37 inches to facilitate patient accessibility and clinician ergonomics. Supports a minimum patient weight capacity of 500 pounds. Includes a three-section upholstered treatment surface to support a variety of patient positioning and therapeutic procedures. Provides an adjustable head section with a positioning range from approximately +45 degrees to -90 degrees. Provides an adjustable lower extremity section with a positioning range from 0 to approximately 78 degrees. Features perimeter foot-operated height controls that allow clinicians to adjust table height from either side while maintaining continuous patient contact. Includes a heavy-duty frame designed to provide stability during patient treatment and transfers. Features four total-lock swivel casters to facilitate movement and secure positioning during patient care. Includes high-density foam cushioning and seamless, heavy-duty upholstered surfaces designed for patient comfort and ease of cleaning. Features rounded table edges and corners to enhance patient safety and reduce the potential for injury. Provides a low transfer height of approximately 18 inches to facilitate patient accessibility and transfers. Operates on standard 120 VAC, 60 Hz electrical service. Includes all power cords, controls, mounting hardware, and accessories necessary for complete clinical operation. Equipment shall be new, current production model equipment suitable for professional healthcare examination, rehabilitation, and therapeutic treatment applications. Interested parties who can provide the products described are requested to submit the following information: Company name, address and point of contact with phone number, SAM Unique Entity Identifier (UEI)*, Product information documenting salient characteristics, Feedback on salient characteristics, Place of manufacture, Socio-economic status to identify the business class as a large business, SDVOSB, VOSB, small business, Woman Owned, etc., and Any other pertinent product, company, or industry information. * Note: To be eligible for award of a federal contract, businesses must have an active registration in the System for Award Management (SAM). Firms that respond to this Sources Sought Notice without providing all the requested information may not be considered by the Government in making acquisition decisions. This market research is conducted for informational and planning purposes only. This notice does not constitute a solicitation and does not obligate the Government to issue a solicitation. The Government, at its sole discretion, may elect not to notify respondents of the results of this notice or otherwise release those results. Send submissions via email to Brian.Rosciszewski@VA.gov, reference 36C25027Q0044 in email subject. Thanks in advance for supporting America s veterans. ** End of Sources Sought Notice **

BACKGROUND AND INFORMATION FOR CONSTRUCTION CONTRACT The New York District, U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (District) is preparing plans and specifications for primarily ecosystem restoration at Liberty State Park, Jersey City, New Jersey. 1. The goal of the project is to create a resilient coastal ecosystem within a highly urbanized setting that provides both ecological and social benefits. Responses to this source sought will be used by the Government to help determine whether the use of a PLA will achieve economy and efficiency in the completion of the subject project. All firms and labor unions should respond to this announcement if they are interested in performing the work for this project. PLA DEFINITION A PLA is defined as a pre-hire collective bargaining agreement with one or more labor organizations that establishes the terms and conditions of employment for a specific construction project and is an agreement described in 29 U.S.C. 158(f). FEDERAL ACQUISITION REGULATION (FAR) SUBPART 22.503 - POLICY Executive Order (E.O.) 14063, Use of Project Labor Agreements for Federal Construction Projects, requires agencies to use project labor agreements in large-scale construction projects to promote economy and efficiency in the administration and completion of Federal construction projects. When awarding a contract in connection with a large-scale construction project (see 22.502), agencies shall require use of project labor agreements for contractors and subcontractors engaged in construction on the project, unless an exception at 22.504(d) applies. An agency may require the use of a project labor agreement on projects where the total cost to the Federal Government is less than that for a large-scale construction project, if appropriate. An agency may, if appropriate, require that every contractor and subcontractor engaged in construction on the project agree, for that project, to negotiate or become a party to a project labor agreement with one or more labor organizations if the agency decides that the use of project labor agreements will Advance the Federal Government's interest in achieving economy and efficiency in Federal procurement, producing labor-management stability, and ensuring compliance with laws and regulations governing safety and health, equal employment opportunity, labor and employment standards, and other matters; and Be consistent with law. Agencies may consider the following factors in deciding whether the use of a project labor agreement is appropriate for a construction project where the total cost to the Federal Government is less than that for a large-scale construction project: The project will require multiple construction contractors and/or subcontractors employing workers in multiple crafts or trades. There is a shortage of skilled labor in the region in which the construction project will be sited. Completion of the project will require an extended period of time. Project labor agreements have been used on comparable projects undertaken by Federal, State, municipal, or private entities in the geographic area of the project. A project labor agreement will promote the agency's long term program interests, such as facilitating the training of a skilled workforce to meet the agency's future construction needs. Any other factors that the agency decides are appropriate. For indefinite-delivery indefinite-quantity (IDIQ) contracts the use of a project labor agreement may be required on an order-by-order basis rather than for the entire contract. For an order at or above $35 million an agency shall require the use of a project labor agreement unless an exception applies. See 22.504(d)(3) and 22.505(b)(3). title: Wireless Telecommunications Carriers (except Satellite)
description: The Contractor shall provide reliable, secure, and high-quality commercial cellular telephone services including voice, messaging, and data throughout Jordan and designated roaming countries. Key elements from the 07 October 2026 PWS include: Service Capabilities: Local and international voice calls; SMS and MMS; internet data; call waiting, call forwarding, three-way calling, and voicemail; tethering; automated SMS usage notifications from the service provider. Feature Authorization: Cellular devices shall be explicitly authorized to utilize only those capabilities specified in the assigned service plan. The Contractor shall disable all unauthorized features. Unauthorized access shall result in no additional expense to the U.S. Government. Coverage: Complete 5G cellular service coverage (or then-current commercial standard, whichever is greater) across the Joint Training Center (JTC), Jordan, including all indoor facilities. Reliable connectivity at all U.S. Government facilities in Jordan. Roaming Network: Single total rate applicable to a special calling group that includes Kuwait, Afghanistan, Iraq, Yemen, Egypt, Jordan, United Arab Emirates, Saudi Arabia, Turkey, Oman, Bahrain, Syria, Djibouti, Lebanon, United States of America, Spain, Germany, United Kingdom, and Ireland. Service Plans: Premium-level plans meeting or exceeding unlimited local incoming/outgoing minutes and SMS/MMS; 150 minutes international/roaming; 150 international/roaming SMS/MMS; 18 GB local and Roaming Network data; tethering; voicemail and advanced calling features. Additional Data Packs (2 GB, 30-day expiration, non-auto-refresh) and MiFi Data plans (10 GB base, incremental 2 GB) required. Service Solutions Applicable to All Users: Accounts configured to prevent overages once plan limits are reached (Contracting Officer may set/remove spend limits); unlimited calling group minutes, SMS, and MMS between users on the account; free incoming/outgoing SMS from the service provider; free incoming international calls deducted from local minutes balance (not charged at an increased rate). SIM Management: Ability to activate, change, or disable individual SIM cards within 12 hours of written notification; free SMS usage alerts at 50%, 75%, 95%, and 100% of monthly allotted call, SMS, and data; trio re-pluggable, three-size form-fit, pre-cut SIM cards; rapid replacement/repair/reimbursement for defective SIMs. Technical & On-Site Support: 24/7/365 technical support with English-language industry-standard trouble tracking; on-site hardware/software support personnel available to arrive within 24 hours of notification; fluent in English including technical terminology; emergency repair response within 24 hours. Network Performance Standards: Network availability ? 99.9% (measured monthly); call setup success rate ? 98%; dropped call rate ? 2%; excellent voice quality with minimal static, echo, or distortion; compliance with primary Quality of Service (QoS) performance obligations in the Contractor�s telecommunications license; service (technology, speed, availability) equivalent to that provided to the Contractor�s commercial customers. Network Survivability and Recovery: Working system of network survivability for emergencies and serious disasters; recovery plan addressing network congestion or partial destruction; online tool for assignment of short numbers, call screening rules, and batch provisioning of directory for Business Group members. Mass Notification: Capability to notify all users on the account via SMS within sixty (60) seconds of initiation. Infrastructure & Maintenance: Capability to enhance coverage via towers, antennas, Cellular-On-Wheels (COWs), repeaters, or in-building solutions at no additional cost to the Government; maintain and refuel fixed and mobile cellular towers; coordinate scheduled maintenance at least seven (7) days in advance. Administrative: WAWF invoicing; online account management portal for the Contracting Officer and authorized representatives; mid-cycle plan changes applied the day of request with prorated charges only (no overlap or double billing); JCCS registration and Combating Trafficking in Persons (CTIP) plan requirements. Note: The full Performance Work Statement (PWS) dated 07 October 2026 will be provided upon request to interested parties that submit a capability statement. The PWS is the authoritative requirements document.

title: Data at Rest (DaR) - 400 Obsolescence Resolution
description: OBJECTIVE: The USAF E-3G AWACS provides worldwide response to situations requiring immediate and continuous on-scene command, control, and battle management using embedded real-time surveillance to support employment of U.S. and allied combat forces. The E-3G consists of the air vehicle, sensor systems, and computing and communications equipment. The current USAF E-3G operational fleet consists of 15 operational aircraft. The E-3G DAR-400 (part numbers 63-2824652-01 through -03) is a mission critical asset and is in critical need of obsolescence resolution to prevent mission impact. Since the DAR-400 contains encrypted MCS, MSS, IPEC and GS data, a failure would directly impact operations and data security. General Dynamics Mission Systems (GDMS) has notified us that the DAR-400 will not be able to support or upgrade to changing NSA requirements. SCOPE: To execute the installation and integration of the obsolescence resolution for the mission-critical E-3G DAR-400 to prevent mission impact. The provided Government-owned KG-204 based solution is compliant with current DoD and NSA mandates to replace the legacy DAR-400 equipment. REQUEST FOR INFORMATION DETAILS: 1. AFLCMC/WIW is requesting information from industry as part of market research to determine interest level and size of qualified vendors. 2. THIS IS A SOURCES SOUGHT ONLY. It is not a Request for Proposal, a Request for Quotation, an Invitation for Bid, a solicitation, or an indication the US Air Force (AF) or AFLCMC/WIW will contract for the items contained in the sources sought. AFLCMC/WIW will not pay respondents for information provided in response to the sources sought. 3. The Government is requesting information from vendors of all business sizes including socioeconomic programs such as 8(a), Historically Underutilized Business Zone (HUBZone), Women Owned Small Business, or Service-Disabled Veteran Owned Small Businesses (SDVOSB) that are interested in performing this requirement. The Government requests interested parties submit a brief description of their company�s business size (i.e., annual revenues and employee size), business status (i.e., 8(a), HUBZone, or SDVOSB, Women Owned Small Business, or small business), and any anticipated teaming arrangements. The Government will use this information in determining its small business set-aside decision. 4. Interested parties should submit a capabilities package, with a cover letter, that is brief and concise yet clearly demonstrates ability to meet the stated requirements with sufficiently qualified personnel. Provide qualification information (type and duration of employee experience relevant to the requirements) and the level of involvement (prime or sub-contractor) and time periods for work on similar projects. The capabilities package should clearly present evidence that the interested party is fully capable of providing the required services and as such may contain any information that the interested party feels relevant. 5. Responses should be submitted electronically, and must be no more than ten single-spaced pages, using 12-point, Times New Roman font, and minimum one-inch margins, in Microsoft Word format. Responses that only provide a company website will not be considered. 6. Responses to the sources sought are requested by 3PM, CDT, 30 October 2026. All responses shall be unclassified and reviewed to ensure consideration. All responses, correspondence, and/or questions related to this matter should be e-mailed to: E-mail: phaedra.prather@us.af.mil Phone: (405) 739-4340 Attachments: DAR 400 Follow On SOW_Sep 2026 DAR Follow-On draft CDRL_DID Package 2026

description: "National Drinking Water Programs Technical, Engineering, and Administrative Support" (NDWPTEAS) The United States Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) Office of Water (OW) is performing a "market search" for large and small businesses in preparation for a future procurement that is a recompete of Contract 68HERC21D0006. The EPA is also interested to see if small businesses are capable of meeting this requirement. Information submitted in response to this notice will only be used for internal market research purposes, and no feedback will be offered to the interested parties that submit capability statements. The subject acquisition is anticipated to provide support services for the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) Office of Ground Water and Drinking Water (OGWDW). OGWDW is responsible for implementing the Safe Drinking Water Act (SDWA), a law which establishes a mandatory national program to protect public health through drinking water safety. In accordance with the SDWA, the EPA is responsible for developing regulations and policies for national drinking water quality. EPA is required to regulate contaminants that present health risks that are either known to or likely to occur in public drinking water supplies that present a meaningful opportunity for health risk reduction. The SDWA Amendments of 1996, as well as several other statutes and executive orders, require that the EPA conduct thorough characterizations of the costs and benefits associated with these regulations. The SDWA requires EPA to identify potential drinking water contaminants, establish criteria for an unregulated contaminant monitoring program, study and gather information on these contaminants, assess whether they require regulation, and review existing regulations every six years and revise as appropriate. Accordingly, the contractors selected under this acquisition shall provide technical, engineering, and analytical support to the EPA consistent with the Performance Work Statement for efforts related to implementing the Safe Drinking Water Act (SDWA). It is expected that this acquisition will be awarded under a full-and-open competition, however market research is still being conducted to determine if there may be small-business set-aside opportunities. The resultant acquisition is anticipated to utilize the Government Services Administration (GSA) Multiple Award Schedule to establish a multiple-awardee Blanket Purchase Agreement (BPA) for up to three vendors. The ordering period is anticipated to be up to five (5) years with a maximum ordering value of $115M with Call Orders issued on a Time-and-Materials (T&M) and/or Fixed Price (FP) basis. To help determine if this potential requirement may be set-aside for small business concerns, the government is seeking input from the small business community regarding their interest and capability in performing the tasks reflected in the attached draft Performance Work Statement (PWS). Vendors are encouraged to use the questionnaire contained in this notice (See Submission Instructions and Capability Information). The applicable North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code is 541620 �Management and Financial Consulting� with a size standard of $19M. Respondents should provide their size status for the above referenced NAICS code, (i.e. large, small) and whether or not they are a certified hub zone, 8(a), women-owned, small-disadvantaged and /or disabled veteran owned concern. In addition, the EPA reserves the right to set the resulting procurement action aside for small businesses. As a reminder, small businesses are required to perform at least 50 percent of the costs of the contract performance with their own personnel (See RFO FAR 52.219-14) under a procurement set aside for small businesses. The Government will review qualifications based on the vendor�s responses with specific emphasis on the vendor�s ability to perform the Scope of Work described in Twelve (12) capability areas in the draft PWS in Section 4. Information submitted in response to this notice is used for internal market research purposes only, and no feedback will be offered to the entities that submit capability statements. For more information and instructions, please see the attachments included with this announcement.

Details of this requirement can be found in the attached Statement of Work (SOW), project/ area maps, and shape files. NAICS: 115310 (Exception 2) - Support Activities for Forestry-Fuels Management PSC: F014 - Natural Resources/ Conservation - Tree Thinning Period of Performance: July 16, 2027 - November 15, 2027 Location: The Crooks Park project area is located approximately 20 miles East of Meeker, CO. description: REQUEST FOR QUOTE Crooks Park Cut & Pile Project Bureau of Land Management Colorado - White River Field Office This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial products or commercial services prepared in accordance with part 12. This announcement constitutes the only solicitation. Offers are being requested and a separate written solicitation will not be issued. Solicitation #140DWF27QL001 is issued as a Request for Quotes (RFQ). This RFQ is being issued as a total set-aside for small business. This solicitation incorporates provisions and clauses by reference. The full text of provisions and clauses may be accessed electronically at www.acquisition.gov. Description Quantity/Acre Unit of Issue Unit Price Total CLIN 0010 Crooks Park Cut & Pile 25 Acre $ $ Description: The Department of the Interior (DOI), Bureau of Land Management (BLM) White River Field Office (WRFO) has a requirement for manual cut & pile of pinyon and juniper trees for the purpose of fuels reduction across approximately 25 acres in the Crooks Park project area. Details of this requirement can be found in the attached Statement of Work (SOW), project/ area maps, and shape files. NAICS: 115310 (Exception 2) - Support Activities for Forestry-Fuels Management PSC: F014 - Natural Resources/ Conservation - Tree Thinning Period of Performance: July 16, 2027 - November 15, 2027 Location: The Crooks Park project area is located approximately 20 miles East of Meeker, CO. Please refer to the attached SOW and area maps for more details. ______________________________________________________________________________ The BLM intends to award a firm fixed-price contract resulting from this RFQ using the lowest price technically acceptable (LPTA) source selection method. In order to be considered technically acceptable, the vendor must demonstrate technical capability and capacity to complete the required work in accordance with the SOW and have satisfactory past performance. In accordance with FAR Part 12 (RFO), offerors must include the following information with your quote submission: 1. Technical Capability (Ability to meet the specifications in the SOW - no longer than 5 pages). 2. Relevant Experience (2 projects ongoing or completed by the prime in the past 5 years) 3. Pricing Note: Any contractor submitting a quote must be registered and active in the System for Award Management (SAM.gov) at the time of submission and potential award. Please include your UEI and CAGE code with your submission. ______________________________________________________________________________ Questions: Please submit any questions via email to the Contracting Officer for this action, David Farina, no later than Friday, October 23, 2026 @ 2:30 PM MT. Site Visit: Site visits can be arranged on an as needed basis. Please contact the COR, Shane Pfeiffer, at 970-620-6957 to confirm the date/time. The deadline for quote submission shall be Friday, October 30, 2026 @ 2:30 PM MT. Quotes received after the deadline will not be considered. All quotes shall be submitted via email to David_farina@ios.doi.gov.

description: The Government is issuing this Sources Sought announcement as a part of market research for the MK-99 Fire Control System (FCS) Program.
