title: Sources Sought for Enterprise Software & Sustainment IDIQ
description: Introduction The Naval Air Systems Command (NAVAIR), Portfolio Acquisition Executive (Aviation) (PAE(A)), is seeking sources to provide comprehensive software and sustainment support for the H-53 (PMA-261), H-60 (PMA-299), and Presidential (PMA-274) helicopter platforms. This effort is for sustaining engineering, program management, logistics, software development and sustainment, flight test support, and fleet readiness for both domestic and Foreign Military Sales (FMS) fleets. Disclaimer THIS ANNOUNCEMENT CONSTITUTES A SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE. THIS SOURCES SOUGHT IS ISSUED AS MARKET RESEARCH SOLELY FOR INFORMATION AND PLANNING PURPOSES � IT DOES NOT CONSTITUTE A REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL (RFP) OR A PROMISE TO ISSUE AN RFP IN THE FUTURE. THIS SOURCES SOUGHT DOES NOT COMMIT THE GOVERNMENT TO AWARD A CONTRACT AS A RESULT OF THIS ANNOUNCEMENT. THESE REQUIREMENTS ARE SUBJECT TO CHANGE AND THE INFORMATION PROVIDED BELOW IS FOR INFORMATIONAL PURPOSES ONLY. THE FINAL REQUIREMENT WILL BE DEFINED UNDER A FORMAL RFP. FURTHER, THE NAVY IS NOT AT THIS TIME SEEKING PROPOSALS AND WILL NOT ACCEPT UNSOLICITED PROPOSALS. RESPONDENTS ARE ADVISED THAT THE GOVERNMENT WILL NOT PAY FOR ANY INFORMATION OR ADMINISTRATIVE COSTS INCURRED IN RESPONSE TO THIS SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE. ALL COSTS ASSOCIATED WITH RESPONDING TO THIS SOURCES SOUGHT WILL BE SOLELY AT THE EXPENSE OF THE INTERESTED PARTY. NOT RESPONDING TO THIS SOURCES SOUGHT DOES NOT PRECLUDE PARTICIPATION IN ANY FUTURE RFP, IF ISSUED. IF A SOLICITATION IS RELEASED, IT WILL BE SYNOPSIZED ON THE FEDERAL BUSINESS OPPORTUNITIES (FBO) WEBSITE. IT IS THE RESPONSIBILITY OF THE POTENTIAL OFFERORS TO MONITOR THIS WEBSITE FOR ADDITIONAL INFORMATION PERTAINING TO THIS REQUIREMENT. Background PAE(A) is establishing an enterprise-wide acquisition solution to consolidate software and sustainment efforts across multiple aviation platforms, including the CH-53K, CH-53E, MH-53E, MH-60R, MH-60S, SH-60B, SH-60F, HH-60H, and Presidential helicopter fleets. The objective is to merge legacy contracts into a single vehicle to secure economies of scale, eliminate duplicative management overhead, and ensure continuous global fleet readiness. Required Capabilities The scope of this effort includes sustaining engineering, program management, logistics, flight test support, training, repairs, reliability improvements, configuration and obsolescence management, system and subsystem software development, and deployed field services. This is a comprehensive requirement to sustain the safety, airworthiness, and operational availability of these critical assets. In order to perform these tasks, respondents must have the following capabilities for the platforms listed above: Demonstrated knowledge of sustaining engineering to include Non-Recurring Engineering (NRE), design, and fleet support for aircraft hardware and software. This includes conducting Engineering Investigations (EIs), managing system interfaces, performing technical analysis, supporting Engineering Change Proposals (ECPs), and managing configuration for CH-53, H-60, and Presidential helicopter platforms. Demonstrated knowledge of software and diagnostics sustainment including full software lifecycle support, including development, deficiency correction, and sustainment for operational flight programs, mission software, and diagnostics applications. Demonstrate experience with laboratory support and managing software requirements, design, qualification, and integration testing. Demonstrated knowledge of logistics support including capability in Product Support Analysis (PSA), including Level of Repair Analysis (LORA) and Maintenance Task Analysis (MTA). Detailed experience with managing Diminishing Manufacturing Sources and Material Shortages (DMSMS), developing and updating Interactive Electronic Technical Manuals (IETMs), and providing provisioning data (DCNs, EDFP). Demonstrated knowledge of system integration and test including test and evaluation support during all phases of hardware and software integration. Describe experience with developing test plans, supporting ground and flight tests, and managing Systems Integration Lab (SIL) environments. Demonstrated knowledge of program management including approach to disciplined systems engineering and program management to support the entire scope of work, including management of subcontractors and complex, multi-platform requirements. Demonstrated knowledge in modifications and installation including detailed experience with kit fabrication, prototype development, and the installation of modifications on aircraft and training devices. Demonstrated knowledge in comprehensive lifecycle support for Foreign and Domestic rotary wing aircraft, including the ability to embed Logistics Support Representatives (LSRs) who can deliver on-site logistics and supply chain management, utilization of Technical Service Representatives (TSRs) to assist with life-limited components, special inspections, and incorporation of modifications, and deployment of Field Service Representatives (FSRs) to provide advanced technical assistance, resolving complex maintenance anomalies and acting as a technical liaison for engineering data and technical deficiency reporting. Eligibility The applicable NAICS code is 336413 with a Small Business Size standard of 1,250 employees. The following product and service codes represent a preponderance of the work; however, additional PSC�s may be utilized at the individual task/delivery order level based on specific requirements being procured. Primary Product Service Codes (PSCs) are 1520 (Aircraft, Rotary Wing), 1680 (Miscellaneous Aircraft Accessories and Components), and J015 (Maint/Repair/Rebuild of Equipment-Aircraft and Airframe Structural Components). Businesses of all sizes are encouraged to respond; however, each respondent must clearly identify their business size. Anticipated Period Of Performance This IDIQ shall have an ordering period of ten (10) years, to include a five-year base period, two, two-year option periods, and one-one-year option period. Requested Information It is requested that interested businesses submit to the contracting office a brief capabilities statement package (no more than 12 pages in length, single-spaced,12 point font minimum) demonstrating ability to perform the tasking listed under the required capabilities. This documentation must address at a minimum the following: Company Name; Company Address; Company Business Size, and Point-of-Contact (POC) name, phone number, fax number, and e-mail address. Company profile to include number of employees, annual revenue history, office location(s), DUNS number, and a statement regarding current small/large business status. Prior/current corporate experience performing efforts of similar size and scope to the tasking described under �Required Capabilities� including contract numbers, contract values, Government point of contact with current telephone number, and a brief description of how the referenced contract related to those tasks. Management approach to staffing this effort with qualified personnel. Specific technical skills company possess which ensure capability to perform the tasks. If you are a small business, provide an explanation of your company�s ability to perform at least 50% of the tasking described in required capabilities, either individually or with any combination of small businesses. Indicate whether you are a large business or qualify as a Small, Small Disadvantaged, Small Disadvantaged Veteran Owned, Small Business Women-Owned, 8(a), Hub Zone or Service Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business Concern. title: USHMM-RFI-2027-MSSP
description: DISCLAIMER / MARKET RESEARCH NOTICE:This Request for Information (RFI) is issued solely for information gathering and planning purposes. It does not constitute a Request for Proposal (RFP), Invitation for Bid (IFB), or an obligation on the part of the United States Holocaust Memorial Museum (USHMM) to acquire any products or services. Responses to this notice are not offers and cannot be accepted by USHMM to form a binding contract. Responders are solely responsible for all expenses associated with responding to this RFI. The United States Holocaust Memorial Museum (USHMM) is conducting formal market research to evaluate commercial vendor capabilities, industry pricing benchmarks, federal/commercial labor rates, and available contract acquisition vehicles (e.g., GSA MAS SIN 54151HACS, NASA SEWP, CIO-SP3/4, SAM.gov) for re-procuring comprehensive Managed Information Technology (IT) Security, Multi-Cloud/DevSecOps Architecture, Network Engineering, and specialized Managed Security Service Provider (MSSP) operational activities. The primary objective of this market research effort is to evaluate whether competitive commercial marketplace capabilities exist to: Sustain, support, and execute day-to-day operations across USHMM's existing "As-Is" securityinfrastructure without operational disruption or increased organizational risk. Perform rigorous security architecture evaluations, threat modeling, gap analyses, and complianceassessments against industry-best security and privacy standards (NIST SP 800-53 r5, FISMA, PCI DSSv4.2.1, CISA Zero Trust Maturity Model, CSF 2.0). Architect and recommend a modernized, cost-effective "To-Be" security state incorporating ZeroTrust architecture, automated orchestration, tool consolidation, and a Government OwnedContractor Operated (GOCO) Security Operations Center (SOC) framework. Execute a seamless, structured transition lifecycle from the "As-Is" state to the "To-Be" operationalmodel within strict schedule and budget parameters. Pricing Benchmarks & Market Rate Expectations Provide feedback on the commercial feasibility of managing this scope under a Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP)monthly fee structure. Provide fully burdened hourly commercial labor rates or GSA schedule rates in the Washington, DCMetropolitan Area for equivalent labor categories (CISO, Security Architect, DevSecOps Engineer,Security Analyst, Network/System Engineer). Submission Instructions & Response Format Response Deadline: All responses shall be submitted electronically no later than October 30, 2026, at 5:00 PM EDT. Submission Format: Responses must be submitted in PDF or Microsoft Word format, strictly limited to no more than fifteen (15) pages (excluding cover page and labor rate tables). Point of Contact: Submissions and any clarifying technical inquiries must be emailed to Mary Green, USHMM Contracting Officer at magreen@ushmm.org with the subject line "RFI Response - USHMM Managed IT Security & MSSP Services".

title: Request for Information on Combat Boot Sock
description: SYNOPSIS: This Sources Sought Announcement is to assist the U.S. Marine Corps Portfolio Acquisition Executive Marine Corps (PAE MC) to identify potential sources to provide a Combat Boot Sock. The goal is to provide warfighting capability and mission support in various environments by enhancing foot comfort, durability, and performance for military personnel. The Government requests that responses be submitted electronically to mary.k.prebensen.civ@army.mil and harvey.walker1@usmc.mil by October 30, 2026 by 5 PM EST. Background: Program Manager Combat Support Systems (PM CSS) is conducting market research to identify potential sources capable of manufacturing a high-performance combat boot sock that meets the requirements of Purchase Description MC-PD-24-003. The sock is intended for use with the applicable standard-issue combat boots identified in the purchase description. This Request for Information (RFI) is issued for market-research and planning purposes only and does not constitute a solicitation, request for proposal, or commitment by the Government to procure any product or service. Description: The Marine Corps is seeking sources capable of manufacturing a durable, reliable combat boot sock designed to provide comfort, protection, and performance during demanding operational use. The sock shall meet the following Salient Characteristics specified in Purchase Description MC-PD-24-003, including, but not limited to, the following key requirements: Sock shall feature an over-the-calf length with cushioning comfort to protect the wearer from hot spots, pressure points, and blisters when wearing combat boots, and they provide graduated compression to promote blood flow from the foot with a non-slip top cuff opening. The foot of each sock includes contouring for the sock to stay in place without bunching, arch support, a gore heel and toe for improved fit, and nylon reinforcement at the heel and toe for durability. A seamless toe closure or a recessed closure with equivalent low profile is used for comfort and durability. Basic Materials. The sock shall contain wool a minimum of 52% wool (no coarser than US 60s (25 microns or finer)), a minimum of 20% nylon, and a minimum of 1% spandex and shall not contain cotton or rayon fiber. Shade. Shall be in accordance with section 3.3 of the Purchase Description Visual shade matching. Shall be in accordance with section 3.4 of the Purchase Description The finished socks shall conform to the requirements specified in table II when tested as specified. **Please refer to Table II. Sock performance requirement** Deliverables: This is a Sources Sought Announcement / RFI to identify potential sources. Based on responses, the Government may plan for a future acquisition. Interested parties should demonstrate their capability to produce socks meeting the above requirements. The Government may request samples for future evaluation. Submission Instructions: THIS IS A SOURCES SOUGHT ANNOUNCEMENT ONLY. This is not a solicitation, and no contract will be awarded from this announcement. Responses are for information and planning purposes only. This Sources Sought Announcement does not constitute a Request for Proposal (RFP) or a promise to issue an RFP in the future. It is subject to change and is not binding on the Government. Further, unsolicited proposals will not be accepted. Funding is not available at this time. The United States Marine Corps has not made a commitment to procure any of the items/services discussed, and release of this Sources Sought Announcement should not be construed as such a commitment or as authorization to incur cost for which reimbursement would be required or sought. Response to this Sources Sought Announcement is voluntary and no reimbursement will be made for any costs associated with providing information in response to this and any follow-on information requests. All submissions become Government property and will not be returned. Not responding to this Sources Sought Announcement does not preclude participation in any future RFP if any is issued. If a solicitation is released, it will be synopsized in the SAM.gov website. It is the responsibility of the potential responders to monitor this site for additional information pertaining to this subject. RESPONSES: Interested parties may identify their interest and capability by sending responses regarding this requirement to PAE MC via e-mail ONLY to harvey.walker1@usmc.mil no later than October 30, 2026 by 5:00 p.m. EST. The U.S. Government will not pay for any information or administrative cost incurred in response to this notice. All costs associated with responding to this Notice will be solely at the expense of the interested party. Please provide business size (indicate your socioeconomic status), applicable NAICS code, and CAGE code. If you hold a GSA Federal Supply Schedule contract, please identify your contract number. QUESTIONS: Any questions for clarification may be emailed to harvey.walker1@usmc.mil no later than October 26, 2026 by 5:00 p.m. EST. Verbal questions will NOT be accepted. Questions shall NOT contain proprietary or classified information. An unattributed list of questions and answers will be published at the same web location of this Sources Sought Announcement.

DAF EMIS Background: The objective of the Department of Air Force Emergency Management Information System (DAF EMIS) is to deliver an enterprise software capability natively deployed within the DoW software ecosystems and data platforms. DAF EMIS will automate and accelerate all four core phases of the Emergency Management lifecycle � Preparedness, Protection, Response, and Recovery � across routine operations, natural disasters, and major contingencies. The purpose of the DAF EMIS is to ensure mission assurance, operational resilience, and timely decision support across the Command and Control (C2) continuum and sustain essential operational missions. description: The U.S. Department of State (DOS) is issuing this Request for Information (RFI)/Sources Sought Notice for market research in accordance with FAR Subpart 10.002(b)(2)(ii) and FAR Subpart 19.501 to gather industry input about the Agency�s requirement, contractor capabilities, and best practices regarding the Office of Security Management�s Administrative Support Division managing the Construction Security Monitoring Program, consisting of Top-Secret Construction Security *Team Leaders (TL), *Assistant Team Leaders (ATL), Cleared American Guards (CAGs), Construction Surveillance Technicians (CSTs), and *Site Security Coordinators (SSC), referred to herein as Site Security Personnel (SSP). *Personnel selected as Team Leaders, Assistant Team Leaders, and Site Security Coordinators will be derived from the base labor categories of CSTs and/or CAGs. DOS is specifically seeking to identify companies that have the skills and capabilities to support this effort, establish suggestions that industry may have to enhance efficiency and improve quality for the performance of these requirements. The DOS also seeks to understand any concerns that industry may have about this requirement. DISCLAIMER This RFI is issued solely for information and planning purposes and does not constitute a Request for Quotation (RFQ), Invitation for Bid (IFB), Request for Proposal (RFP), or an obligation on the part of the Government to acquire any services. Responses to this RFI are not offers and will not be accepted by the Government to form a binding contract of any nature. The Government will not award a contract because of this notice. The Government does reserve the right to determine how it will proceed because of this notice. Your response will assist the Government in the development of its acquisition strategy for a possible Request for Proposal (RFP) which may be issued later. This notice will also help with determining whether any type of small business set-aside is possible for this procurement or whether full and open competitive procedures should be utilized. If full and open competition is ultimately pursued, responses to this synopsis will be used to aid in establishing small business subcontracting goals. Responding parties should not anticipate Government feedback on their respective submissions. The Government will not pay any cost incurred in response to this RFI. All costs associated with responding to this RFI will be solely at the responding party�s expense. It is the responsibility of the potential contractors to monitor the websites for any information that may pertain to this RFI or future solicitation. All information requested and received in response to this RFI will be treated as information only. The information provided in this RFI is subject to change and is not binding on the Government. DOS plans to review and meaningfully consider all responses to this RFI. Also, it must be advised that all submissions become Government property and will not be returned. Proprietary information and trade secrets, if any, should be minimized and must be clearly marked on all materials. Responses to this RFI may be reviewed by Government technical experts drawn from staff within DOS and/or by selected support contractor personnel. All Government and support contractors will be bound by appropriate non-disclosure agreements to protect proprietary and source selection information as described in 41 USC 423. The Government shall not be held liable for any damages incurred if proprietary information is not properly identified. GENERAL INFORMATION Current Contract Information: Incumbent contractors are currently providing construction security services at Department of State facilities abroad. This includes, but is not limited to, professional monitoring of uncleared labor, observation and note taking, reporting of all security violations, site access control, 24/7 presence, material inspection, document control, and assistance to the designated Site Security Manager(s). Contract Type: The Government contemplates award of either Labor Hours, Time and Material, Firm Fixed Price, or a combination of contract types. Estimated Contract Value: $250M Period of Performance: The period of performance of the contract is anticipated from March 15, 2027, through March 14, 2032, with a one (1)-year Base Period and four (4) one (1)-year Option Periods. NAICS Code: The anticipated North American Industry Code System (NAICS) code for this procurement is 561612, Security Guards and Patrol Services. PROGRAM DESCRIPTION The Department of State (DoS) requires the implementation of SSP to support operations at various overseas facilities designed to control unauthorized access to controlled areas, to deter the introduction of unauthorized materials to the compound, site, or building, and to surveil the activities of un-cleared construction workers to prevent the implantation of clandestine surveillance devices or systems into the structure or its surroundings. REQUIRED CAPABILITIES To be considered capable, interested sources must demonstrate the capability to meet all the following requirements set forth herein: Task 1.0 Recruitment of Personnel The contractor shall be capable of recruiting personnel qualified to obtain the necessary security clearance and having the minimal eligibility requirements for each labor category: Construction Surveillance Technicians must have at least five (5) years� experience in at least one, or a combination of construction security surveillance, technical surveillance countermeasures, industrial or government security involving counterintelligence, construction quality assurance, hands-on construction supervisory or significant construction experience, or Military Occupational Specialty (MOS) relating to any of the requirements. Cleared American Guards must have three years� experience as or like a Military Policeman, Marine Security Guard (MSG), or a security watch stander whose duties included the use of alarm systems, metal detectors, x-ray devices and closed-circuit television systems. Team Leaders and Site Security Coordinators must be approved by the CSM Program Office (COR). They will be evaluated on a case-by-case basis by regard to task order solicitation request and requirements. All personnel must be 21 years of age and older. Task 1.1 Personnel Capabilities All personnel must be in adequate physical and mental health; validated by a licensed physician, and be capable of working within construction sites that include, but are not limited to experiencing: hazardous air quality without personal protective equipment (PPE), standing and walking for extended periods of time, navigating terrain that may present the need to climb, withstand slippery conditions, capable of ascending/descending scaffolding up to 75ft, and able to work in inclement weather and harsh environments. All personnel must be capable of reading, (legible) writing, and conveying information in English. Task 2.0 Training The contractor is required to provide a syllabus and execute training to cover a variety of topics to include at a minimum: situational awareness, leadership training, social media awareness, note taking, mental health awareness, and other categories related to this type of work. Task 3.0 ClearancesThe Contractor shall maintain a Top-Secret Facility Clearance issued by DCSA until completion of the contract. Loss of facility clearance will result in termination of the contract for cause. All personnel submitted to work on task orders, including the Program Manager and Deputy Program Manager, shall hold a TS clearance and be submitted for a DOS Reciprocal Top-Secret Clearance. Task 4.0 Accounting All contractors shall have an accounting system in place to meet DCAA Compliance standards, which include, but are not limited to: Segregation of direct and indirect costs Cumulative-to-date direct costs by CLIN Segregation and identification of unallowable costs Total time

title: Integrated Logistics Division (ILD) Maintenance and Logistics Support Services
description: This public posting is for informational, planning, and market research purposes only and constitutes a Request for Information (RFI) and a Sources Sought Request (SSR) only for United States, Department of Homeland Security (DHS), Customs and Border Protection (CBP). This announcement does not constitute a commitment, implied or otherwise, that a solicitation or procurement will be issued. This is not a solicitation, Request for Proposal (RFP), or Invitation for Bids (IFB). No reimbursement will be made for any costs associated with providing information in response to this announcement or any follow-up information requests. No questions will be addressed at this time. As a component of the United States (U.S.) Department of Homeland Security (DHS), Customs and Border Protection (CBP) is responsible for protecting our Nation�s borders in order to prevent terrorists and terrorist weapons from entering the U.S. while facilitating the flow of legitimate trade and travel. CBP is also responsible for apprehending individuals attempting to enter the U.S. illegally; stemming the flow of drugs and other contraband; protecting our agricultural and economic interests from harmful pests and diseases; protecting American business from theft of their intellectual property; and regulating and facilitating international trade, collecting import duties, and enforcing U.S. trade laws. In support of this responsibility CBP has implemented and deployed numerous technology systems across the U.S. and internationally that require systems administration and maintenance services. ILD manages a 24/7 Maintenance Dispatch Center for maintenance activities. The Maintenance Dispatch Center (MDC) initially responds to service calls from the numerous CBP sites. The Maintenance Dispatch Center staff record the calls for service in the CBP databases ServiceNow and Integrated Logistics Support System, i.e., MAXIMO). Maintenance Dispatch Center staff issue requests for repair or maintenance services to the Contractor in the form of a Work Order (WO) that initiates the maintenance request. The Contractor responds to the CBP sites, effects repair or completes maintenance actions and provides periodic status updates and Work Completion Forms (WCF) to the Maintenance Dispatch Center based on the provided requirements contained in this Performance Work Statement. SCOPE The Contractor shall provide labor, services, equipment, parts, consumables, supplies, packaging, transport, shipment, and materials required to maintain NII and RDE Technologies (mobile, fixed, and portable) identified in this contract. This equipment includes accessories, peripherals, information technologies, and vehicle chassis, and control booth equipment and accommodations where applicable, that was identified during CBP site acceptance. This support is required at CONUS and OCONUS CBP locations and includes configuration management, warranty transitions, preventive maintenance, corrosion control, customer support/trouble call handling, corrective maintenance, system administration services, and failure trend/root cause analysis. Other requested on-demand maintenance and support services may include engineering, site surveys, parts provisioning, retrofits, relocations, source change outs, disposal, maintenance and operator refresher training, special event support, and emergency services on an occasional and emergent need basis. INSTRUCTIONS Interested parties are encouraged to respond to this notice if they have the capability and capacity to provide the identified services. The RFI process is an important part of CBP�s market research as required by the Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR). Among other things, to justify a small business or 8(a) set-aside procurement, CBP�s market research must demonstrate that there are at least two small businesses or 8(a) small businesses capable of performing at a fair and reasonable price that are likely to submit offerors. Respondents need to list their current contract vehicles and whether or not they are a small business, Historically Underutilized Business Zone, Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business, 8(a) small business, Women-Owned Small Business, or small disadvantaged business. The due date and time for responses is no later than 5:00 PM ET, October 30, 2026. The RFI/SSR responses shall be submitted electronic via email to all the following team members via a group email on or before the response date with the subject line "Integrated Logistics Division Maintenance and Logistics Support Services RFI�: Contract Specialist, Debbie Dean, Email debbie.d.dean@cbp.dhs.gov Contracting Officer, Monica Watts, Email monica.y.watts@cbp.dhs.gov All responses must adhere to the page limits of 10 pages total. The submission shall be logically assembled. Each response section shall be clearly identified and shall begin at the top of a page. All pages of each response section shall be appropriately numbered and identified by the complete company name, date, and referenced number listed on the Notice in the header and/or footer.

description: DISCLAIMER / MARKET RESEARCH NOTICE:This Request for Information (RFI) is issued solely for information gathering and planning purposes. Responses to this notice are not offers and cannot be accepted by USHMM to form a binding contract. Responders are solely responsible for all expenses associated with responding to this RFI. The United States Holocaust Memorial Museum (USHMM) is conducting formal market research to evaluate commercial vendor capabilities, industry pricing benchmarks, federal/commercial labor rates, and available contract acquisition vehicles (e.g., GSA MAS SIN 54151HACS, NASA SEWP, CIO-SP3/4, SAM.gov) for re-procuring comprehensive Managed Information Technology (IT) Security, Multi-Cloud/DevSecOps Architecture, Network Engineering, and specialized Managed Security Service Provider (MSSP) operational activities. The primary objective of this market research effort is to evaluate whether competitive commercial marketplace capabilities exist to: Sustain, support, and execute day-to-day operations across USHMM's existing "As-Is" securityinfrastructure without operational disruption or increased organizational risk. Perform rigorous security architecture evaluations, threat modeling, gap analyses, and complianceassessments against industry-best security and privacy standards (NIST SP 800-53 r5, FISMA, PCI DSSv4.2.1, CISA Zero Trust Maturity Model, CSF 2.0). Architect and recommend a modernized, cost-effective "To-Be" security state incorporating ZeroTrust architecture, automated orchestration, tool consolidation, and a Government OwnedContractor Operated (GOCO) Security Operations Center (SOC) framework. Execute a seamless, structured transition lifecycle from the "As-Is" state to the "To-Be" operationalmodel within strict schedule and budget parameters. Pricing Benchmarks & Market Rate Expectations Provide feedback on the commercial feasibility of managing this scope under a Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP)monthly fee structure. Provide fully burdened hourly commercial labor rates or GSA schedule rates in the Washington, DCMetropolitan Area for equivalent labor categories (CISO, Security Architect, DevSecOps Engineer,Security Analyst, Network/System Engineer). Submission Instructions & Response Format Response Deadline: All responses shall be submitted electronically no later than October 30, 2026, at 5:00 PM EDT. Submission Format: Responses must be submitted in PDF or Microsoft Word format, strictly limited to no more than fifteen (15) pages (excluding cover page and labor rate tables). Point of Contact: Submissions and any clarifying technical inquiries must be emailed to Mary Green, USHMM Contracting Officer at magreen@ushmm.org with the subject line "RFI Response - USHMM Managed IT Security & MSSP Services".

title: CAMP WOOTEN/STARBUCK LEVEE REHAB
description: 1. BACKGROUND This sources-sought announcement is a tool to identify businesses with the capability to accomplish the work. This is not a solicitation. This notice neither constitutes a Request for Proposal, nor does it restrict the Government to an ultimate acquisition approach. It should not be construed as a commitment by the Government for any purpose. Responses to this Sources Sought notice will be used for market research purposes by the Government to make appropriate acquisition decisions. Therefore, no contract award will result from this Sources Sought Notice. The United States Army Corps of Engineers (USACE), Walla Walla District, is seeking interested business sources for a levee rehabilitation construction project entitled: Camp Wooten/Starbuck Levee Rehab. Both the Starbuck and Camp Wooten Levee�s are located on the Tucannon River near the town of Starbuck, and Camp Wooten respectively. Both locations are in Columbia County, State of Washington. This will be a firm fixed price construction contract. North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code for this project is: 237990 - Other Heavy and Civil Engineering Construction. The associated small business size is $45 million. Performance and Payment Bonds will be required. Responses to this Sources Sought Notice should include the following information: A list of current or past projects demonstrating technical experience with work of a similar nature to that listed in the Summary Scope of Work. For each project submitted, provide a brief narrative statement of the work involved, your firm's role in the project, performance period, the dollar value and the completion date. Include a statement detailing any special qualifications and certifications, applicable to the scope of this project, held by your firm and/or in-house personnel. If any of the experience is that of a subcontractor, please specify that information in your response. A reference list for each of the projects submitted in A) above. Include the name, title, phone number and email address for each reference. Provide a statement of your firm's business size (Large, HUBZone, Service Disabled Veteran Owned, 8(a), small disadvantaged, or woman-owned) with regards to the NAICS code listed above. Provide the percentage of work you (as the prime) intend to perform. If you intend to subcontract a major portion of the work (defined as at least 20% of the work), please include this information in your response. Provide a statement that your firm intends to submit a bid on the project when it is advertised. Provide a statement of your firm's bonding capacity. A statement from your surety is not required. CAGE Code and SAM.GOV Unique Entity ID. Companies or individuals interested in responding are invited to submit their information via email ONLY to Nathan Bruce at: nathan.i.bruce@usace.army.mil. All attachments must be provided in either Microsoft Word or Adobe Acrobat PDF format. Responses should be received by 2:00 p.m. PDT, 30 October 2026. PLEASE REFERENCE "SOURCES SOUGHT: Camp Wooten/Starbuck Levee Rehab" IN THE SUBJECT LINE. Respondents will not be contacted regarding their submission or information gathered as a result of this sources sought notice. All responsible sources may respond to this notice and all responses will be considered. Telephonic responses will not be honored. 2. SUMMARY SCOPE OF WORK Starbuck Levee The levee is located on the right levee bank of the Tucannon River in the vicinity of the Kellogg Hollow Road Bridge, Columbia County, Washington, near the town of Starbuck. Flood flows significantly scoured and eroded one site approximately 280 feet upstream of the Kellogg Hollow Road Bridge. Flood fight operations were performed by Columbia County during the flood event. The scour area is approximately 150' long and extends into the crown of the levee. The second damaged area is approximately 550' downstream of the Kellogg Hollow Road Bridge. The downstream site did not receive flood fight operations and is approximately 20' long. Rehab will include reconstruction of levee portions that have eroded and replacement of armoring on the riverward side of the levee portions to restore levees to pre-damage conditions. Camp Wooten Levee The levee is located on the right levee bank of the Tucannon River, Columbia County, Washington, near Camp Wooten, a Washington State Park Retreat Center. One discrete damage site with a length of roughly 160 feet was identified and reported by the inspection team. Damages observed in this area is attributable to scour and erosion of the levee toe. This has left the levee slope vulnerable to further damage. Rehab will include restoration to the as-was condition by reestablishing riverside slope where erosion has taken place and armoring with riprap. This involves re-constructing portions of the levee that eroded away, including the levee toe. USACE expects to award a single contract in December 2026. The expected work window for the Camp Wooten Levee is January 2027 � February 2027, and for the Starbuck Levee between February 2027 � March 2027. The Camp Wooten magnitude of construction is estimated to be between $500,000 and $1,000,000. The Starbuck magnitude of construction is estimated to be between $1,000,000 and $5,000,000. All on-site work shall be performed in accordance with the USACE Safety and Health Requirements Manual (EM 385-1-1). The Contractor will be responsible for establishing and managing an effective on-site Safety and Health program in accordance with EM 385-1-1 that will require the development and submission of a comprehensive project specific Accident Prevention Plan for Government acceptance. In addition, the Contractor will be required to develop and submit for Government acceptance an Activity Hazard Analyses, for each phase of work that complies with EM 385-1-1. A Site Safety and Health Officer (SSHO) employed by the prime contractor shall be required for each shift of the contractor's on-site operations. The SSHO shall possess a minimum of 3-years of experience in construction safety on similar projects and shall have completed the 30-Hour OSHA Construction Safety training within the last 5-years. A Certified Erosion and Sediment Control Lead employed by the prime contractor will choose and install erosion control materials for specific site conditions, as necessary. The Contractor will be required to use the Government-furnished Construction Contractor Module (referred to as QCS) of the Resident Management System (RMS) to record, maintain, and submit various information throughout the contract period. QCS is a Windows-based program that can be run on a stand-alone personal computer or on a network. The Government will make the QCS software available to the Contractor after contract award.

title: Request for Information on Combat Boot Sock
description: SYNOPSIS: This Sources Sought Announcement is to assist the U.S. Marine Corps Portfolio Acquisition Executive Marine Corps (PAE MC) to identify potential sources to provide a Combat Boot Sock. The goal is to provide warfighting capability and mission support in various environments by enhancing foot comfort, durability, and performance for military personnel. The Government requests that responses be submitted electronically to mary.k.prebensen.civ@army.mil and harvey.walker1@usmc.mil by October 30, 2026 by 5 PM EST. Background: Program Manager Combat Support Systems (PM CSS) is conducting market research to identify potential sources capable of manufacturing a high-performance combat boot sock that meets the requirements of Purchase Description MC-PD-24-003. The sock is intended for use with the applicable standard-issue combat boots identified in the purchase description. This Request for Information (RFI) is issued for market-research and planning purposes only and does not constitute a solicitation, request for proposal, or commitment by the Government to procure any product or service. Description: The Marine Corps is seeking sources capable of manufacturing a durable, reliable combat boot sock designed to provide comfort, protection, and performance during demanding operational use. The sock shall meet the following Salient Characteristics specified in Purchase Description MC-PD-24-003, including, but not limited to, the following key requirements: Sock shall feature an over-the-calf length with cushioning comfort to protect the wearer from hot spots, pressure points, and blisters when wearing combat boots, and they provide graduated compression to promote blood flow from the foot with a non-slip top cuff opening. The foot of each sock includes contouring for the sock to stay in place without bunching, arch support, a gore heel and toe for improved fit, and nylon reinforcement at the heel and toe for durability. A seamless toe closure or a recessed closure with equivalent low profile is used for comfort and durability. Basic Materials. The sock shall contain wool a minimum of 52% wool (no coarser than US 60s (25 microns or finer)), a minimum of 20% nylon, and a minimum of 1% spandex and shall not contain cotton or rayon fiber. Shade. Shall be in accordance with section 3.3 of the Purchase Description Visual shade matching. Shall be in accordance with section 3.4 of the Purchase Description The finished socks shall conform to the requirements specified in table II when tested as specified. **Please refer to Table II. Sock performance requirement** Deliverables: This is a Sources Sought Announcement / RFI to identify potential sources. Based on responses, the Government may plan for a future acquisition. Interested parties should demonstrate their capability to produce socks meeting the above requirements. The Government may request samples for future evaluation. Submission Instructions: THIS IS A SOURCES SOUGHT ANNOUNCEMENT ONLY. This is not a solicitation, and no contract will be awarded from this announcement. Responses are for information and planning purposes only. This Sources Sought Announcement does not constitute a Request for Proposal (RFP) or a promise to issue an RFP in the future. It is subject to change and is not binding on the Government. Further, unsolicited proposals will not be accepted. Funding is not available at this time. The United States Marine Corps has not made a commitment to procure any of the items/services discussed, and release of this Sources Sought Announcement should not be construed as such a commitment or as authorization to incur cost for which reimbursement would be required or sought. Response to this Sources Sought Announcement is voluntary and no reimbursement will be made for any costs associated with providing information in response to this and any follow-on information requests. All submissions become Government property and will not be returned. Not responding to this Sources Sought Announcement does not preclude participation in any future RFP if any is issued. If a solicitation is released, it will be synopsized in the SAM.gov website. It is the responsibility of the potential responders to monitor this site for additional information pertaining to this subject. RESPONSES: Interested parties may identify their interest and capability by sending responses regarding this requirement to PAE MC via e-mail ONLY to harvey.walker1@usmc.mil no later than October 30, 2026 by 5:00 p.m. EST. The U.S. Government will not pay for any information or administrative cost incurred in response to this notice. All costs associated with responding to this Notice will be solely at the expense of the interested party. Please provide business size (indicate your socioeconomic status), applicable NAICS code, and CAGE code. If you hold a GSA Federal Supply Schedule contract, please identify your contract number. QUESTIONS: Any questions for clarification may be emailed to harvey.walker1@usmc.mil no later than October 26, 2026 by 5:00 p.m. EST. Verbal questions will NOT be accepted. Questions shall NOT contain proprietary or classified information. An unattributed list of questions and answers will be published at the same web location of this Sources Sought Announcement. **Amendment 0001 - attachment uploaded to answer questions**

description: Cadaver-Based Medical Training & Program Support The Medical Acquisition Support Office � Alpha (MASO-A) has issued a Sources Sought Notice to identify capable vendors that can deliver Human Cadaver - Based Medical Training and Program Support Services for the 44th Medical Brigade stationed at Fort Bragg Army Base, North Carolina. The scope of this upcoming procurement is requiring the contractor to provide human cadavers, medical equipment, Class VIII Supplies, training days, transportation/logistical support, Subject Matter Expert (SME) and cadaver medical training support. Additionally, the selected source will be responsible for administering cadaver medical training and program support. The contract structure is anticipated to consist of a base period of performance accompanied by four subsequent one-year option periods. THIS IS NOT A SOLICITATION ANNOUNCEMENT � This is a Sources Sought Notice issued solely for information and planning purposes, and it does not constitute a Request for Quote (RFQ) or a promise to issue a solicitation in the future. Solicitations are not available at this time and requests for a solicitation will not receive a response. This notice does not commit the United States Government to contract for any supply or service whatsoever. All information submitted in response to this announcement is entirely voluntary; the Government will not pay for the information requested, nor will it compensate any respondent for costs incurred in developing their response. Furthermore, not responding to this Sources Sought Notice does not preclude participation in any future RFQ, should one be issued. Potential offerors are solely responsible for monitoring this site for any updates or additional information pertaining to this requirement. Finally, the Government encourages and welcomes vendor questions to help us better understand industry standards and market capabilities concerning this Cadaver-Based Medical Training & Program Support Requirement. The Government will utilize all received responses to formulate its acquisition strategy; however, if the Government does not receive sufficient information in response to this notice to verify that a potential for competition exists, a sole-source contract, supported by a Justification and Approval document, may be issued to support this requirement. Consequently, (MASO-A) is seeking the specific capability and business details outlined in the following paragraph to determine market capacity and evaluate prospective sources for this Cadaver Training Services Requirement. Company name, DUNS number, CAGE code, and point of contact information (including phone number and email address), and socio-economic category(ies) as related to NAICS 621991 (Blood and Organ Banks), such as 8(a), HUBZone, Women-Owned, Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned, Small, or Other-than-Small. Capability Statement (limited to ten pages), describing how your company meets the objectives below, providing additional proof (such as FDA approval) where appropriate: Our customer, the 44th Medical Brigade stationed at Fort Bragg, North Carolina, requires training and support services to include the procurement of human cadavers, medical equipment, Class VIII Supplies, training days, transportation/logistical support, Subject Matter Expert (SME) support, and cadaver medical training support necessary to execute their medical readiness mission. Basic Requirements: The contract must include capability to provide human cadavers, medical equipment, Class VIII Supplies, training days, transportation/logistical support, Subject Matter Expert (SME) support, and cadaver medical training support. Cadaver Specimens: The contractor must be able to provide up to 20 non-dissected perfused cadaveric specimens annually to support trauma sustained training events. The contractor shall be capable of supporting events with 2 to 6 cadavers per event. The contractor shall procure and deliver ethically sourced high-quality human cadaver specimens that meet the following criteria: All specimens shall be whole-body, non-prosected, fresh or preserved with a formalin-free solution, aged between 20-65 years, and weigh ? 250 lbs. All specimens must be serologically negative for HIV-1/2, Hepatitis B/C, and Syphilis. The contractor shall provide documented negative test results and full chain-of-custody documentation upon delivery. The vendor/supplier of the cadaveric specimens must ensure all state and U.S. territory laws and regulations applicable to the use and/or transport of cadavers are followed. The use of each specimen must be consistent with the donor�s intent, as documented on the donor authorization form. The vendor/supplier of the cadaveric specimens must be certified by the American Association of Tissue Banks (AATB), or an equivalent accrediting body. Training Days: The contractor shall be capable of supporting training events for a minimum of two training days. title: M872A4 Trailer Pre-Cut Wood
description: SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE / REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) Notice Type: Sources Sought Notice / Market Research Procurement Title: Pre-Cut Wood Decking Floor Kits for M872A4 Semitrailers Requiring Activity: Combined Support Maintenance Shop (CSMS) 1, Montgomery, AL Supported Unit: 781st Transportation Company Response Window: 7 Calendar Days from Date of Publication Response Deadline: 30 October 2026, 4:00 PM Central Standard Time (CST) Anticipated NAICS Code: 321918 � Other Millwork (including Flooring) (or 321999 � All Other Miscellaneous Wood Product Manufacturing) Product Service Code (PSC): 2510 � Vehicular Cab, Body, and Frame Structural Components (or 2540 / 5510) 1. DISCLAIMER AND GENERAL INFORMATION This is a Sources Sought Notice / Request for Information (RFI) issued solely for market research, information, and planning purposes in accordance with FAR Part 10 (Market Research). This announcement does not constitute a Request for Proposal (RFP), Request for Quote (RFQ), Invitation for Bid (IFB), or an obligation that the Government will issue a formal solicitation. The Government will not award a contract on the basis of this notice, nor will it reimburse respondents for any costs incurred in preparing or submitting responses. Responses will assist the Government in determining the availability of commercial items, competitive market capabilities, and potential small business set-aside strategies (e.g., Small Business, 8(a), SDVOSB, WOSB, HUBZone). 2. BACKGROUND AND SCOPE OF REQUIREMENT The Combined Support Maintenance Shop (CSMS) 1 located in Montgomery, Alabama, has an operational requirement to procure high-durability, pre-cut wood decking floor packages to support maintenance, overhaul, and refurbishment of forty (40) M872A4 40-Ton Semitrailers in direct support of the 781st Transportation Company. All forty (40) trailers must be fully mission-capable, inspected, and safety-certified prior to scheduled unit movement. Summary of Items CLIN 0001: Pre-Cut Decking Floor Kits for M872A4 Trailers Quantity: 40 Complete Kits Description: Complete vehicle-set wood packages containing all pre-cut, profiled, and drilled boards necessary for the 100% full deck replacement of one (1) standard 40-foot M872A4 flatbed trailer per kit. 3. TECHNICAL SPECIFICATIONS & STANDARDS All delivered items must strictly conform to Technical Manual TM 9-2330-381-14&P (and associated Bill of Materials / layout specifications): Requirement Area Specification Standard Material Type & Quality Apitong (Keruing) hardwood boards, graded as "Select or Better". Moisture Content Kiln-dried with a delivered moisture content between 12% and 15%. Trailer Compatibility Standard M872A4 40-Ton Semitrailer (40-foot flatbed layout). Dimensions & Machining Exact board dimensions, cuts, edge profiles, shiplap/tongue-and-groove configurations, and countersinks must match TM 9-2330-381-14&P specifications without requiring on-site cutting or re-machining. Kit Contents Forty (40) standalone kits. Each kit must include the complete complement of wood components needed for a single trailer overhaul. Warranty & Manuals Standard commercial/manufacturer warranty against defects in material and workmanship under normal military use; applicable technical data and product care documentation included. 4. PLACE OF PERFORMANCE AND DELIVERY SCHEDULE Delivery Location: Combined Support Maintenance Shop (CSMS) 1 1720 Congressman W.L. Dickinson Dr. Montgomery, AL 36109 Delivery Timeline: Delivery Commencement / First Shipment: 20 November 2026 Final Delivery Deadline (NLT): 31 January 2027 Deliveries must follow a phased arrival schedule to accommodate shop throughput and inspection capacity. Inspection & Acceptance: Government inspection and acceptance will take place upon delivery at CSMS 1. Each delivery must be accompanied by a comprehensive Bill of Lading (BOL) / delivery packing slip itemizing contents and kit batch identifiers. 5. CAPABILITY STATEMENT & SUBMISSION REQUIREMENTS Interested commercial vendors and manufacturers capable of fulfilling this requirement are invited to submit a Capabilities Statement (maximum 5 pages) addressing the following areas: A. Vendor Identification & Profile Company Name, Address, and Website. Unique Entity Identifier (UEI) and CAGE Code. Primary Point of Contact (Name, Title, Phone, and Email). Business Size and Socioeconomic Status under NAICS 321918 / 321999 (e.g., Large Business, Small Business, SDB, WOSB, SDVOSB, HUBZone). Existing Government-wide Contract Vehicles (e.g., GSA MAS, DLA, OASIS), if applicable. B. Technical & Manufacturing Capability Material Sourcing & Milling: Confirm access to genuine Apitong (Keruing) hardwood graded "Select or Better" and capability to achieve kiln-dried moisture levels of 12�15%. Technical Compliance: Describe capability to manufacture, precision-cut, profile, and countersink lumber in exact compliance with military specifications (TM 9-2330-381-14&P). Packaging: Ability to package and palletize the boards into 40 distinct, ready-to-assemble vehicle kits. C. Schedule & Logistical Capacity Confirm ability to meet the required delivery performance window: initial delivery on 20 November 2026 and completion no later than 31 January 2027 at Montgomery, AL. Identify current production lead times and any known supply chain vulnerabilities for Apitong lumber. D. Rough Order of Magnitude (ROM) & Commercial Practices Provide non-binding Rough Order of Magnitude (ROM) pricing per kit or total estimated cost for 40 kits. Detail standard commercial warranty terms, customary packaging methods, and shipping practices. 6. SUBMISSION INSTRUCTIONS Due Date & Time: All responses must be received within seven (7) calendar days of this notice, no later than 30 October, at 4:00 PM CST. Submission Format: Electronic format via email (PDF or MS Word format). Subject Line Format: Response to Sources Sought: M872A4 Decking Kits - [Company Name] Submissions Shall Be Sent To: Primary Contracting POC: Kathryn Graham, Contract Specialist / Contracting Officer Email: kathryn.p.graham.civ@army.mil Phone: 334-450-0463 Note: Proprietary information, if submitted, must be clearly marked. The Government will handle proprietary materials in accordance with applicable Federal Acquisition Regulations.

title: Cleared American Guards(CAGs)and Construction Surveillance Technicians (CSTs)
description: The U.S. Department of State (DOS) is issuing this Request for Information (RFI)/Sources Sought Notice for market research in accordance with FAR Subpart 10.002(b)(2)(ii) and FAR Subpart 19.501 to gather industry input about the Agency�s requirement, contractor capabilities, and best practices regarding the Office of Security Management�s Administrative Support Division managing the Construction Security Monitoring Program, consisting of Top-Secret Construction Security *Team Leaders (TL), *Assistant Team Leaders (ATL), Cleared American Guards (CAGs), Construction Surveillance Technicians (CSTs), and *Site Security Coordinators (SSC), referred to herein as Site Security Personnel (SSP). *Personnel selected as Team Leaders, Assistant Team Leaders, and Site Security Coordinators will be derived from the base labor categories of CSTs and/or CAGs. DOS is specifically seeking to identify companies that have the skills and capabilities to support this effort, establish suggestions that industry may have to enhance efficiency and improve quality for the performance of these requirements. The DOS also seeks to understand any concerns that industry may have about this requirement. DISCLAIMER This RFI is issued solely for information and planning purposes and does not constitute a Request for Quotation (RFQ), Invitation for Bid (IFB), Request for Proposal (RFP), or an obligation on the part of the Government to acquire any services. Responses to this RFI are not offers and will not be accepted by the Government to form a binding contract of any nature. The Government will not award a contract because of this notice. The Government does reserve the right to determine how it will proceed because of this notice. Your response will assist the Government in the development of its acquisition strategy for a possible Request for Proposal (RFP) which may be issued later. This notice will also help with determining whether any type of small business set-aside is possible for this procurement or whether full and open competitive procedures should be utilized. If full and open competition is ultimately pursued, responses to this synopsis will be used to aid in establishing small business subcontracting goals. Responding parties should not anticipate Government feedback on their respective submissions. The Government will not pay any cost incurred in response to this RFI. All costs associated with responding to this RFI will be solely at the responding party�s expense. It is the responsibility of the potential contractors to monitor the websites for any information that may pertain to this RFI or future solicitation. All information requested and received in response to this RFI will be treated as information only. The information provided in this RFI is subject to change and is not binding on the Government. DOS plans to review and meaningfully consider all responses to this RFI. Also, it must be advised that all submissions become Government property and will not be returned. Proprietary information and trade secrets, if any, should be minimized and must be clearly marked on all materials. Responses to this RFI may be reviewed by Government technical experts drawn from staff within DOS and/or by selected support contractor personnel. All Government and support contractors will be bound by appropriate non-disclosure agreements to protect proprietary and source selection information as described in 41 USC 423. The Government shall not be held liable for any damages incurred if proprietary information is not properly identified. GENERAL INFORMATION Current Contract Information: Incumbent contractors are currently providing construction security services at Department of State facilities abroad. This includes, but is not limited to, professional monitoring of uncleared labor, observation and note taking, reporting of all security violations, site access control, 24/7 presence, material inspection, document control, and assistance to the designated Site Security Manager(s). Contract Type: The Government contemplates award of either Labor Hours, Time and Material, Firm Fixed Price, or a combination of contract types. Estimated Contract Value: $250M Period of Performance: The period of performance of the contract is anticipated from March 15, 2027, through March 14, 2032, with a one (1)-year Base Period and four (4) one (1)-year Option Periods. NAICS Code: The anticipated North American Industry Code System (NAICS) code for this procurement is 561612, Security Guards and Patrol Services. PROGRAM DESCRIPTION The Department of State (DoS) requires the implementation of SSP to support operations at various overseas facilities designed to control unauthorized access to controlled areas, to deter the introduction of unauthorized materials to the compound, site, or building, and to surveil the activities of un-cleared construction workers to prevent the implantation of clandestine surveillance devices or systems into the structure or its surroundings. REQUIRED CAPABILITIES To be considered capable, interested sources must demonstrate the capability to meet all the following requirements set forth herein: Task 1.0 Recruitment of Personnel The contractor shall be capable of recruiting personnel qualified to obtain the necessary security clearance and having the minimal eligibility requirements for each labor category: Construction Surveillance Technicians must have at least five (5) years� experience in at least one, or a combination of construction security surveillance, technical surveillance countermeasures, industrial or government security involving counterintelligence, construction quality assurance, hands-on construction supervisory or significant construction experience, or Military Occupational Specialty (MOS) relating to any of the requirements. Cleared American Guards must have three years� experience as or like a Military Policeman, Marine Security Guard (MSG), or a security watch stander whose duties included the use of alarm systems, metal detectors, x-ray devices and closed-circuit television systems. Team Leaders and Site Security Coordinators must be approved by the CSM Program Office (COR). They will be evaluated on a case-by-case basis by regard to task order solicitation request and requirements. All personnel must be 21 years of age and older. Task 1.1 Personnel Capabilities All personnel must be in adequate physical and mental health; validated by a licensed physician, and be capable of working within construction sites that include, but are not limited to experiencing: hazardous air quality without personal protective equipment (PPE), standing and walking for extended periods of time, navigating terrain that may present the need to climb, withstand slippery conditions, capable of ascending/descending scaffolding up to 75ft, and able to work in inclement weather and harsh environments. All personnel must be capable of reading, (legible) writing, and conveying information in English. Task 2.0 Training The contractor is required to provide a syllabus and execute training to cover a variety of topics to include at a minimum: situational awareness, leadership training, social media awareness, note taking, mental health awareness, and other categories related to this type of work. Task 3.0 ClearancesThe Contractor shall maintain a Top-Secret Facility Clearance issued by DCSA until completion of the contract. Loss of facility clearance will result in termination of the contract for cause. All personnel submitted to work on task orders, including the Program Manager and Deputy Program Manager, shall hold a TS clearance and be submitted for a DOS Reciprocal Top-Secret Clearance. Task 4.0 Accounting All contractors shall have an accounting system in place to meet DCAA Compliance standards, which include, but are not limited to: Segregation of direct and indirect costs Cumulative-to-date direct costs by CLIN Segregation and identification of unallowable costs Total time

description: SYNOPSIS: #N68335-27-R-1002 TEST SET � ELECTRONIC SEQUENCER Naval Air Warfare Center Aircraft Division - VFC-204 Standup Effort At NOLA The Naval Air Warfare Center, Aircraft Division (NAWCAD) Lakehurst, NJ intends to negotiate on a sole source basis with Teledyne Risi, Inc., CAGE: 0EUB8 for the Test Set � Electronic Sequencer hardware components in support of the NAWCAD VFC-204 Standup Effort At NOLA. This order will procure one (1) Electronic Sequencer Test Set. The Electronic Sequencer Test Set eliminates false removal errors for the Navy Aircrew Common Ejection Seats (NACES) ejection sequencer and allows for true failures. This item is used to expand the test tolerance of the TTU-515/E to account for pressure transducer cyclic drift and update the internal electronics to accommodate the fast sequencer. In addition, six percent of the NACES ejection sequencers are currently being rejected during the SDLM servicing and this item will eliminate those failures. Teledyne Risi, Inc., as the Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM) of the Electronic Sequencer Test Set, is the only source with the requisite knowledge, technical experience, and production-level data to produce these components. The components being procured are integral to the NACES ejection sequencer systems and are critical to maintaining operational readiness. The Government intends to solicit and negotiate this requirement under the authority of 10 U.S.C. 2304(c)(1), FAR 6.302-1 - Only one responsible source and no other supplies or services will satisfy agency requirements. THIS NOTICE IS NOT A REQUEST FOR COMPETITIVE PROPOSALS. However, the Government will consider all responses received within fifteen days after the date of publication of this synopsis. title: USHMM-RFI-2027-MSSP
description: DISCLAIMER / MARKET RESEARCH NOTICE:This Request for Information (RFI) is issued solely for information gathering and planning purposes. It does not constitute a Request for Proposal (RFP), Invitation for Bid (IFB), or an obligation on the part of the United States Holocaust Memorial Museum (USHMM) to acquire any products or services. Responses to this notice are not offers and cannot be accepted by USHMM to form a binding contract. Responders are solely responsible for all expenses associated with responding to this RFI. The United States Holocaust Memorial Museum (USHMM) is conducting formal market research to evaluate commercial vendor capabilities, industry pricing benchmarks, federal/commercial labor rates, and available contract acquisition vehicles (e.g., GSA MAS SIN 54151HACS, NASA SEWP, CIO-SP3/4, SAM.gov) for re-procuring comprehensive Managed Information Technology (IT) Security, Multi-Cloud/DevSecOps Architecture, Network Engineering, and specialized Managed Security Service Provider (MSSP) operational activities. The primary objective of this market research effort is to evaluate whether competitive commercial marketplace capabilities exist to: Sustain, support, and execute day-to-day operations across USHMM's existing "As-Is" securityinfrastructure without operational disruption or increased organizational risk. Perform rigorous security architecture evaluations, threat modeling, gap analyses, and complianceassessments against industry-best security and privacy standards (NIST SP 800-53 r5, FISMA, PCI DSSv4.2.1, CISA Zero Trust Maturity Model, CSF 2.0). Architect and recommend a modernized, cost-effective "To-Be" security state incorporating ZeroTrust architecture, automated orchestration, tool consolidation, and a Government OwnedContractor Operated (GOCO) Security Operations Center (SOC) framework. Execute a seamless, structured transition lifecycle from the "As-Is" state to the "To-Be" operationalmodel within strict schedule and budget parameters. Pricing Benchmarks & Market Rate Expectations Provide feedback on the commercial feasibility of managing this scope under a Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP)monthly fee structure. Provide fully burdened hourly commercial labor rates or GSA schedule rates in the Washington, DCMetropolitan Area for equivalent labor categories (CISO, Security Architect, DevSecOps Engineer,Security Analyst, Network/System Engineer). Submission Instructions & Response Format Response Deadline: All responses shall be submitted electronically no later than October 30, 2026, at 5:00 PM EDT. Submission Format: Responses must be submitted in PDF or Microsoft Word format, strictly limited to no more than fifteen (15) pages (excluding cover page and labor rate tables). Point of Contact: Submissions and any clarifying technical inquiries must be emailed to Mary Green, USHMM Contracting Officer at magreen@ushmm.org with the subject line "RFI Response - USHMM Managed IT Security & MSSP Services".

description: Department of Veterans Affairs Tennessee Valley Healthcare System (TVHS) Alvin C. York Campus Intent to Sole Source Thompson Machinery Commerce Corporation The Department of Veterans Affairs intends to issue sole-source firm-fixed priced contract to Thompson Machinery Commerce Corporation, 1245 Bridgestone Pkwy, La Vergne, TN 37086. A sole source procurement will be issued as an Open Market Purchase Order to Thompson Machinery Commerce Corporation. This procurement is being conducted in accordance with FAR RFO 12.102-1(b). In the interest of economy and efficiency, the Original Equipment Manufacturer (Caterpillar Inc.), stated only one exclusive Small Business (SB), Thompson Machinery Commerce Corporation is the only Factory Authorized source for Sales, Service, and Parts for Caterpillar Equipment in Middle & West Tennessee, and Northern Mississippi areas. In addition, All Caterpillar, Inc, software for engine controls and emissions adjustments are proprietary. The NAICS code is 333120 and has a size standard of 1,250 employees for this procurement. Project Requirements: Reoccuring Full-Service Maintenance and Rebuild Contract on the Caterpillar G3520C Generator Set and Associated System. Background: TVHS VA Medical Center a full-service maintenance and rebuild contract on the Caterpillar G3520C Generator Set and Associated Radiator System located in Building 16. The Caterpillar G3520C, Serial # GZL00146 Generator set is a natural gas fueled engine that has very strict maintenance requirements for continuous and reliable operation. The plant has been in operation for over 10 years and has logged 52,299+ hours of operation, the generator set has been under a service contract with Thompson Power/Caterpillar. The generator sets purpose is to provide primary electrical power and steam to the facility to reduce the cost of the electrical utility and increase utility efficiency, it does work. The engine will have an in-frame overhaul based on hours operated and will be under a 1-year warranty by Caterpillar. The engine requires maintenance at the manufacturers specified intervals to ensure proper operating characteristics as well as continuation of the servicing contractor s warranty. Maintenance is of utmost importance for reduced operational costs and to ensure the longevity of the generator set s life expectancy. Scope of work: The contractor is to provide manufacturer s authorized/certified service technicians, transportation, equipment, maintenance parts, materials, specialty tools and supervision to provide the manufacturer s required maintenance services to ensure proper and continuous operation of the Caterpillar G3520C generator set radiator system and auxiliary systems connected to the engine. Daily checks will be performed by VA boiler plant employees. This maintenance contract is to include all items required to be checked, inspected, measured, tested, serviced, or replaced at defined intervals in the manufacturer s service manual, SEBU7681-16 dated November 2010 and will include any manufacturer s updated requirements. This contract will include the following requirements not fully specified in the Caterpillar service manual: maintenance free battery replacement on or before 24-month installation/replacement anniversaries, 1000-hour equipment run time/service interval exterior cleaning the radiator system of accumulated dust and debris, inspection of fluid level indicators and fluid replacement as needed, lubricating fan bearings and fan belt inspection and replacements. radiator interior flushing, coolant replacement, accessory drive belts and all coolant system hose replacement, thermostats and gaskets, radiator caps at/or before 5-year recommended intervals. The contractor is to provide all parts, materials and labor for 1 (one) standard top end overhaul, 18,000 service hours or multiples thereof. 1 (one) out of frame overhaul (including top end overhaul) within the manufacturers recommended service hours during the 5th year period of this service contract (option year 4). The contractor shall provide labor, transportation, tools, parts and materials to rebuild or replace some serviceable parts as described in the requirements section of the Statement of Work (SOW). Parts found during the overhauls considered to be defective or worn that are not included in the recommended overhaul procedures or specified in the requirements section below will be paid for under a repair purchase order and are not the contractor s financial responsibility to replace under this agreement. The contractor will provide a list of parts the manufacturer requires to be replaced under the overhauls for clarification of the top end, in frame and out of frame rebuild requirements.
